title: DFL appoints HBS’ Wistuba to lead Sportcast brodacast production
article_text:
German soccer’s DFL league organizer has announced the appointment of experienced sports broadcast director Stefan Wistuba as the new chief executive (CEO) of its in-house production arm, Sportcast.

Wistuba will join the Sportcast managing board (which unanimously selected him for the role) on May 1, 2027, for a transitionary period before taking over the CEO role in full on June 30, replacing the outgoing Josef Nehl.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Nehl is retiring after what will be a 21-year stint at the helm of Sportcast, having overseen operations at the business since it was founded.

Speaking on the leadership shift, Sportcast supervisory board chair and Bundesliga chief executive Steffen Merkel said: “Josef Nehl has not only led Sportcast for more than two decades, but has also built up the company since its foundation and played a decisive role in shaping it.

“With his vast experience, high standards of quality and keen sense of technological developments, he has made a significant contribution to raising the media production of the Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 to the very highest international standards.

“In Stefan Wistuba, we have also found the right successor to continue this successful development and to further advance Sportcast within a dynamically changing media and technology landscape.

Sportcast, which was created in 2006, oversees the TV production of all top-flight Bundesliga and second-tier 2. Bundesliga matches, as well as all games in the DFB Pokal knockout tournament and the Super Cup, and coordinates international broadcast signal distribution for rights holders in over 200 countries.

Wistuba joins from Host Broadcast Services (HBS), the television production company owned by international sports marketing agency Infront, after 18 years at the organization.

He joined HBS in August 2028 as production and project manager for a range of its contracted FIFA soccer tournaments, including the FIFA World Cup 2010 in South Africa, and the FIFA Women's World Cup 2011 in Germany.

Following that, he took up similar production management roles for the FIFA World Cups in 2014 (Brazil) and 2018 (Russia), as well as the 2015 Women’s World Cup (Canada), before becoming head of production in 2017.

Wistuba eventually rose to the role of director of production (2019 to 2024), and is now the director of the FIFA projects unit, having also been the project director for the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the US, Canada, and Mexico, which featured more games than any previous World Cup.

In his new role, he will work alongside incumbent Sportscast managing director Alexander Günther.

Merkel continued: “Stefan Wistuba has many years of experience and proven expertise in the media and production sectors, as well as a strong spirit of innovation. Together with Alexander Günther and the entire team, he will successfully drive Sportcast’s development forward and provide important impetus for the company’s future.”

title: Revolut under judicial administration: what is at stake for its Audi F1 sponsorship
article_text:
In my view, in the short term, almost nothing. On 16 November 2026 a Milan court placed the Italian branch of Revolut, the bank that gives its name to the Audi Revolut F1 Team, under judicial administration for one year. The court granted the request of the Milan public prosecutor’s office, which alleges serious shortcomings in the bank’s anti-money-laundering controls. The bank stays open, though, and the order is not a conviction: that is why I believe Audi will leave the contract alone. The real risk lies in communications, because for a bank the product is trust.

Suppose you are the head of communications at a Formula 1 team. One morning the name written on your car is in the headlines for a reason that has nothing to do with overtaking. What do you do? Do you take the logo off before the next race? Do you ring the sponsor to find out what it is going to say? Do you put out a statement? Or do you wait, hoping the story slides down the page?

Formula 1 has been here before, more often than you might think. Motorsport has always had a soft spot for people who handle money: banks, finance houses, cryptocurrency platforms, people who love speed almost as much as we do. Every so often, though, one of them comes under a judge’s scrutiny, and the answers given over the years say a good deal about what to expect now.

What did the Milan court decide about Revolut?

On 16 November 2026 the preventive measures section of the Court of Milan ordered one year of judicial administration for the Italian branch of Revolut Bank, the Revolut group’s Lithuanian bank. The order was requested by the Milan public prosecutor’s office and carried out by the Guardia di Finanza, Italy’s financial police.

The issue is anti-money-laundering controls. For anyone who does not work in a bank, these are the checks a bank must carry out to understand who its customers are and where their money comes from. According to prosecutors, Revolut’s controls in Italy were so weak that people under investigation, or already convicted, were able to use the bank’s accounts. Some of them are alleged to have links to organised crime, and tens of millions of euros are alleged to have passed through those accounts. The criminal investigations concern these customers; the measure imposed on the bank is there to fix the controls.

Revolut has said that it acknowledges the decision, that it will cooperate fully with the Italian authorities and that its banking services in Italy continue to operate normally, with no interruption for customers. This is not the first time someone has taken a close look at its controls. In April 2025 the Bank of Lithuania fined Revolut Bank €3.5 million for shortcomings in the monitoring of customer transactions.

Judicial administration: what does it mean for a bank that sponsors Formula 1?

It means that for one year the bank works with two court-appointed administrators at its side, who check and correct its procedures. It is a preventive measure under article 34 of Italy’s anti-mafia code (Legislative Decree 159/2011): it does not establish criminal guilt and it does not close the company, which carries on operating. The sponsor, in other words, carries on doing its job.

The Court of Milan has already used this measure on some very well-known companies. In April 2024 it was the turn of Giorgio Armani Operations, and in June of Manufactures Dior, over a failure to check suppliers where labour exploitation had come to light. In both cases the measure was lifted in February 2025, ahead of schedule, after the companies had overhauled their controls.

The case closest to Revolut’s, because it involves a bank, is that of Banca Progetto. In October 2024 the court placed it under judicial administration over loans granted to companies linked to a person arrested in 2023 in an investigation into the ‘Ndrangheta. In July 2025 the measure was lifted early. In the meantime, however, in March 2025 the Bank of Italy, the country’s central bank, had put it into special administration under a separate order: the court lifting its measure did not put an end to the bank’s problems.

For Revolut, in my view, these are the precedents that matter, far more than the Formula 1 ones we will come to in a moment. They tell us two things: that a measure like this can be closed early, and that the court is not the only referee. How it ends will depend on what the administrators find and on how quickly the bank puts things right.

When a financial sponsor has run into trouble, how have Formula 1 teams handled the communications?

In three different ways. As I see it, the choice almost always came down to a single question: can the sponsor still pay, and is it still presentable? When the answer was no, the team cut ties within hours. When it was yes, the team either managed the exit or carried on regardless. On the blog you will also find six F1 sponsorships that failed and the story of crypto sponsorship, from the boom to the collapse of FTX.

On 11 November 2022 FTX, the cryptocurrency platform that sponsored Mercedes, filed for bankruptcy protection in the United States. That same day Mercedes suspended the deal, and at the Brazilian Grand Prix the cars raced without the logo. Toto Wolff said that “partners like us” had been left in “utter disbelief”. “We considered FTX,” he said, “because they were one of the most credible and solid, financially sound partners that were out there.” The matter did not end there. In November 2023 a group of investors sued the company behind the team, accusing it of promoting unregistered financial products without checking closely enough who it was promoting. As far as is known, there is still no ruling that concerns the team.

title: International Swimming League agrees global rights deal with DAZN
article_text:
The International Swimming League (ISL), the club-based professional series, has announced a global media rights agreement with major sports streaming platform DAZN.

Through the agreement, DAZN will be responsible for the worldwide distribution of the league's upcoming relaunch event, the ISL All-Star Match.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The one-night event takes place at the London Aquatics Centre in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park on December 19.

The All-Star Match will be live and free globally on DAZN, in English, on a non-exclusive basis, outside several reserved territories where dedicated local broadcast arrangements will be announced separately.

DAZN will broadcast the event across its 200 markets.

The All-Star Match will see the world's fastest swimmers compete in a team-based, two-hour, head-to-head competition.

Four teams will compete, based on a geographical principle: the United States, the Commonwealth, Europe, and the rest of the world, each made up of the leading athletes from their region.

The ISL will unveil further broadcast and distribution partners “in the coming weeks.”

Ben Allen, commissioner of the International Swimming League, said: “The All-Star Match is built to be watched, and this agreement means fans almost anywhere in the world can do so live and free.

“DAZN is the home of some of the biggest sports on the planet, and swimming’s return to the ISL stage belongs in that company.”

Last month, the ISL appointed Gravity Media as its broadcast content and production partner ahead of its relaunch.

The ISL’s comeback campaign will see as many as seven fixtures staged in venues across North America, Europe, Asia, and potentially the Middle East next year.

It will feature a refined format, with the trial of a one-day event concept, as opposed to the prior two-day edition.

Late last year, ISL commissioner Ben Allen explained that this relaunch will come with a revamped commercial and funding model aimed at ensuring the sustainability of the series, which was suspended in 2022 after the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which hampered the business interests of primary investor Konstantin Grigorishin.

Grigorishin, the founder and chair of the ISL, remains involved, but the series is also now drawing on a wider range of revenue streams, particularly sponsorship and broadcast income, to ensure its commercial model is more balanced going forward, and to further insulate it from geopolitical shocks such as the war in Ukraine and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The series was initially conceived as a means of maintaining interest in swimming annually outside of the Olympics.

In its initial iteration, the ISL attracted high-profile names such as Olympic champions Adam Peaty and Katinka Hosszú, but those same swimmers have also been mired in lawsuits related to antitrust concerns against the World Aquatics governing body.

It faced a legal dispute with FINA (now World Aquatics) during 2018 and 2019, with the governing body having initially refused to allow athletes to compete in it as an unsanctioned series and then launching its own direct competitor.

As with other sports around the world, the ISL then faced disruption during 2020, its second season, because of the coronavirus pandemic, as well as further associated legal difficulties.

With the lawsuits seemingly settled and new backing secured, a roadmap for the return of the ISL was created.

Allen also stated his hope that the momentum surrounding the LA28 Olympic Games and swimming’s position at the games could help to bolster interest in the series.

title: SMU agrees to helmet sticker sponsorship with Visit Dallas for rest of 2026 season
Karren Brady and Nathan Thompson launch sports agency
article_text:
Former West Ham United Vice-Chairman Baroness Karren Brady CBE has joined forces with Nathan Thompson to launch Brady Thompson, a new agency aiming to unlock hundreds of millions of pounds in untapped commercial value across UK sport and entertainment.

The agency will focus on three areas: originating and securing high-value commercial partnerships, transforming corporate hospitality and its revenue potential, and advising brands on strategy across sport and entertainment.

Brady brings decades of boardroom experience across sport, entertainment, media and business. As well as her time at West Ham, she is a Member of the House of Lords and Lord Sugar’s business adviser on the BBC’s The Apprentice.

Thompson is a senior executive and board-level leader whose experience spans sponsorship, brand partnerships, venues, marketing and commercial development. When he left West Ham, he was one of only two Black board members in the Premier League.

Baroness Karren Brady CBE, Co-Founder of Brady Thompson, said, “Sport and entertainment have never been more commercially powerful. Audiences are global, brands are increasingly recognising the value of being part of that world, and the commercial opportunities are enormous. Yet there remains a significant gap between the value organisations are currently generating and what they could achieve.“

She adds,“Unlocking that potential takes more than simply selling sponsorship or hospitality. It takes commercial imagination, experience, relationships, the right processes and, above all, the bravery to challenge convention. That is what Brady Thompson is here to deliver.”

The agency launches as rights holders face growing pressure to maximise their commercial assets, while brands look for more sophisticated ways to connect with audiences. Its approach centres on identifying opportunities others overlook and turning them into measurable commercial outcomes.

Nathan Thompson, Co-Founder of Brady Thompson, said, “I’ve sat in boardrooms on every side of these deals – as a sales executive, an adviser and a board member. I understand what rights holders need to achieve commercially, and I understand what brands are looking for when they invest in sport and entertainment. The real opportunity lies in bringing those two worlds together in a way that creates genuine value for both. Brady Thompson has been built to do exactly that.”

title: British Cycling Ventures and Koru team up
article_text:
British Cycling Ventures has formed a joint venture with Koru Sports Group to drive the commercial growth of the City of London Nocturne, with plans to take the closed-road race to more UK cities.

The event returns on 11th-12th June 2027 at the Square Mile Race Circuit, a 1.4km course that winds through Cheapside and Bank with the Royal Exchange and the City skyline as its backdrop. Elite day and night racing runs alongside a street party of live music, food stalls and entertainment, with riders of all ages and abilities taking part.

The 2026 edition was broadcast live and featured a family-friendly programme including the Penny Farthing Race, the Brompton Folding Bike Race and the new Voi Bike Challenge.

The venture aims to expand the Nocturne nationally and give teams and riders new opportunities, while complementing the domestic racing structure, including the Lloyds National Circuit Series. It will focus on fan experience, new audiences in key urban markets and a strong commercial programme.

The move follows growing momentum for cycling in the UK. Thousands of fans lined the streets for this year’s Lloyds Tour of Britain Women and Men, and tickets for December’s UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup in Glasgow have been in high demand.

Darren Henry, Managing Director of British Cycling Ventures, said, “This is another significant moment in the major events vision of British Cycling Ventures, and the commercial growth of major city racing in the UK. “

“The innovation and plans for growth of the Nocturne from Koru Sports Group is significant for cycling in the country, and this joint venture brings together the best expertise in our sport to deliver huge impact through high-quality events. After hosting a brilliant event in the heart of London this year, it will continue to produce a spectacular atmosphere for riders and fans alike and make it an event not to be missed.”

James Pope of Koru Sports Group said, “I’ve been privileged to have been organising cycling events for over two decades in the UK and have worked closely with British Cycling during this time. The plans and ambition of British Cycling Ventures present an exciting opportunity to introduce a new major city racing concept in the UK starting with the City of London Nocturne. This partnership will help us create a new world class city event format that will be a major boost to the UK racing scene, creating a fantastic experience for riders and cycling fans.”

title: Cadillac F1 signs Viatris as pharmaceutical partner
article_text:
The Cadillac Formula 1 Team, which ran its debut season from its base at Silverstone, has signed healthcare company Viatris to a multi-year partnership starting in 2027.

Although Cadillac is billed as America’s new Formula 1 team, Silverstone is at the heart of its operation. While construction of its US headquarters in Fishers, Indiana, is completed, the team has run its 2026 campaign mainly from the Northamptonshire facility. The base houses its logistics as well as its aerodynamic and mechanical design. The team has committed to keeping the facility for at least ten years, giving it access to the experienced talent of the UK’s Motorsport Valley.

Viatris will become the team’s global pharmaceutical partner from the 2027 season, Cadillac’s second on the grid. The partnership links motorsport and medicine, two industries where precision, reliability and performance matter.

Viatris marks its sixth anniversary this year. It was formed in 2020 through the combination of Mylan and Upjohn, a former division of Pfizer, and has since delivered medicines to patients in more than 165 countries and territories. Its portfolio covers generics, value-added medicines, established brands and innovative medicines.

Viatris’s UK business is headquartered in Hatfield, Hertfordshire, and supplies medicines to patients across the country.

Tyler Epp, Global Head of Commercial Strategy at Cadillac Formula 1 Team, said, “Viatris makes medicines that people count on every day, and Formula 1® gives them one of the biggest stages in the world to show how they do it. For a team in its first season, having a global company like Viatris choose to partner with the Cadillac Formula 1® Team says a lot about where we’re headed. We are thankful for the trust that Viatris has placed in our team and cannot wait to grow with them into the future.”

Andrew Enrietti, Chief Administrative and Transformation Officer at Viatris, said, “What attracted us to the Cadillac Formula 1® Team is the ambition and ingenuity behind what they’re building. At Viatris, we’re focused on executing our strategy and continuing to find ways to make a difference for patients around the world.“

“We share a determination to embrace new opportunities, bring talented people and different perspectives together, and turn bold ideas into meaningful progress. This partnership gives us an exciting opportunity to showcase that shared spirit while introducing Viatris to new audiences around the world.”

Viatris joins the group of global companies that partnered with the team in its first season. The team is backed by TWG Motorsports and General Motors, and its wider commercial programme will grow as the Fishers headquarters opens in 2027. It aims to become a full-works American team by the end of the decade. Excel Sports Management, the team’s agency of record, supported the partnership discussions.

title: Ezpeleta: MotoGP valued ‘reach before fees’ in ESPN deal
article_text:
MotoGP is prioritising reach over rights fees with its new US broadcast deal with ESPN, according to the series’ deputy chief executive Carlos Ezpeleta.

Last week, the global motorcycling series signed a two-year media rights deal with the Disney-owned broadcaster across the US and Latin America. This is MotoGP’s first broadcast deal in the former since its takeover by Liberty Media.

Beginning in 2027, MotoGP races will air on ESPN networks and platforms in the United States, either live or on same-day delay. Across Latin America, ESPN will continue to provide extensive MotoGP coverage, including streaming on Disney+.

MotoGP has partnered with ESPN in Latin America since 2002 and this new agreement also enables the broadcaster so sublicense select events in Argentina and Brazil to local free-to-air broadcasters.

However, the US market is still underdeveloped for MotoGP. Ezpeleta told SportsPro that the first priority is “to just get our wonderful sport in front of more eyeballs”.

He added: “The most important thing that we valued in this deal and in this market is just reach before fees. … Investments in a sport come in many shapes and sizes, and picking the best possible media partners is one of those investments, sometimes it’s picking visibility and reach.”

The short-term nature of the deal also ensures MotoGP can properly evaluate the market before renegotiating for the 2029 season and beyond.

“In a more mature market, you need more time to actually make a significant change in percentage,” said Ezpeleta. “We’re going into ESPN without knowing what that bar is. So again, we have our own numbers but we’re sure that it will be a success.”

ESPN was Formula One’s media rights partner in the US before its transition to Apple TVthis season, so having that industry knowledge from within Liberty helped the negotiation process.

“[Liberty chief executive] Derek Chang knows everybody at ESPN, and then of course we have on our board Chase Carey and Sean Bratches, so all of those people are very well known to ESPN,” confirmed Ezpeleta.

“Obviously, the deals always have to make sense from a negotiation standpoint, but being able to leverage those voices and really getting that buy-in from ESPN is very valuable.”

At the same time, Ezpeleta is clear that MotoGP is trying to do things its own way. While the series is technically following the Formula One playbook in the US, the Spaniard maintained that “MotoGP and Formula One are two different brands”.

Ezpeleta also confirmed that VideoPass will still be available to the US market despite this new deal with ESPN as the US “is actually our biggest single market for VideoPass” and ESPN will be more focused on providing top-of-funnel access.

And looking to the future, Ezpeleta is hopeful that a successful media rights deal will lead to more race opportunities for MotoGP in the US.

“Long term we would be looking to add when the time is right, and especially when the destination is right, a destination within the US that’s additive, that’s reaching a different type of fan,” he said.

Until then, success will be measured by the number of eyeballs drawn to the sport, something Ezpeleta hopes will then “transfer to success in all of our revenue streams”.

title: Stena Line and Special Olympics Ireland Mark First Year of Partnership
article_text:
Stena Line and Special Olympics Ireland marked the first anniversary of their partnership by celebrating the athletes, volunteers and communities supported through the sponsorship over the past 12 months.

The partnership was launched in November 2025 and is built around a shared belief in the power of sport to change lives and create greater inclusion.

To mark the anniversary, Stena Line crew welcomed three Special Olympics Ireland athletes onboard Stena Estrid, where they joined broadcaster Marie Crowe in reflecting on what the partnership has meant to them.

Each was asked to choose one word to describe the relationship, with empowerment, togetherness, equality and opportunity among those selected.

Stena Line captain Master Jack Deurden chose “inspiring”, highlighting the impact that meeting Special Olympics athletes has had on the ship’s crew.

“It’s a pleasure for us to meet the athletes, to welcome them onboard and show them around the ship,” he said.

“The dedication and resilience they display really is inspiring, and it’s great to be able to have a chat with them, learn a bit about their journey and understand what it takes for these athletes and their families to achieve what they have.”

Special Olympics Ireland athlete Carrie Doyle said the organisation had played an important role in building her own confidence.

“The Special Olympics has taught me to be a stronger person and has improved my confidence.

“I would like to thank Stena Line for welcoming us on board, showing us the beautiful boat and for listening to us talk about our experience.”

Stena Line’s support is helping Special Olympics Ireland provide almost 7,000 athletes across the island with access to training, competition and personal development opportunities, from local club activity through to representing Ireland internationally.

The partnership played a visible role at this year’s Special Olympics Ireland Summer Games. Over 1,200 athletes and 2,500 volunteers took part in the largest inclusive sports event staged here since the World Games in 2003.

Stena Line supported the recruitment and deployment of those volunteers without whom the Games would not have been possible.

Johan Edelman, Trade Director for Stena Line, said the first year had reinforced the values shared by both organisations.

“We’re honoured to support Special Olympics Ireland and play a part in the journey of these incredible athletes as they make a real difference in local communities across Ireland.

“We’ve been inspired by the dedication and hard work they have displayed throughout the past 12 months.

“Inclusivity and care are an important part of the Stena Line way, and the Special Olympics Ireland Summer Games were incredible.

“We’re all excited to see the athletes prepare for the Special Olympics World Summer Games in Santiago, Chile next year.”

“Partnerships like this go far beyond funding sport; they change lives, strengthen communities, and champion inclusion across Ireland,” said Karen Coventry, CEO of Special Olympics Ireland.

“We are deeply grateful to Stena Line for their continued support and for being such an important part of this journey.”

The partnership provides sponsorship that supports the impact which the Special Olympics has across the country.

It also delivers moments of inspiration for the company and its staff that are hard to put a value on.

Special Olympics Ireland is a full member of the Sport for Business Community. If you would like to join them and see your organisation in our content, on our stages, and in the daily conversation around the commercial world of Irish Sport, email us today and let’s see what is possible.

Sport for Business is Ireland’s leading platform focused on the commercial, strategic and societal impact of sport. It connects decision-makers across governing bodies, clubs, brands, agencies, and public institutions through high-quality content, events, and insights.

Sport for Business explores how sport drives economic value, participation, inclusion and national identity, and how your story can be part of ours.

Through analysis, storytelling and convening the sector, it helps leaders understand trends, share best practices, and make better-informed decisions. It positions sport not just as entertainment but as a vital contributor to Ireland’s social and economic fabric.

title: Steve Borthwick and Fabien Galthie underline importance of respect for officials after Rassie Erasmus comments
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

England head coach Steve Borthwick and France counterpart Fabien Galthie have emphasised the importance of upholding respect for match officials after South Africa’s Rassie Erasmus was banned for six matches.

Erasmus, who has led the Springboks to back-to-back World Cup wins, was suspended for a third time having made comments that questioned the integrity of officials earlier this week.

The 54-year-old, previously banned by World Rugby in 2021 and 2022, made reference to “match-fixing” in wide-ranging comments as he sought to draw attention to what he perceived as double standards within the sport after South Africa’s defeat to France and Ireland’s win over Fiji.

The Springboks take on Andy Farrell’s side on Dublin on Saturday evening, with Erasmus – banned from matchday involvement – intending to run a live stream from his hotel room of his reactions to the game.

While wishing not to directly comment on Erasmus’s remarks, both Borthwick and Galthie used their team announcement press conferences to underline the values of rugby they believe should be maintained.

“In the world of coaching, I have a duty of conscience towards the fans, towards the coaches, towards the players,” Galthie explained. “I have a duty and a responsibility towards the world of rugby, towards World Rugby. When you hold the position of head coach, you are responsible for your words, responsible for your behaviour.

“As a coach, I have to take care of the refereeing. If I don't take care of the referees, if I talk about referees, then I hurt rugby, I hurt the supporters, I hurt our opponents. The first thing we learn in our sport is fair play. We shake hands with the opponent and arrange to meet for the next match, for the next fight. There's always this idea of honour and fair play. That's how I learned it at rugby school, to say 'Mr referee’, shake his hand at the end of the match, take care of him.

"You have to be careful because rugby is a sport that is heavily refereed. More than half of the actions are stopped or whistled by an official. Without a referee, there is no rugby. There is no rugby among children, there is no education, since we have to respect a rule.”

Echoing a similar theme, Borthwick underscored the difficult role that referees have.

“What I will say is that match officials have a really tough job,” the England head coach stressed. “It's a really challenging job that match officials have.

“Number two, I have absolute 100 per cent confidence and faith that every match official in every game tries to do the very best they can. And, number three, I think they deserve enormous respect. And that's the way in rugby, you respect the match officials; any player or coach, we expect the same.

“In the values of our game, respect is clearly central to that. You call the referee ‘Sir’. And I still do now, it has been a habit for so many years, you call the referee ‘Sir’. It doesn’t mean we always agree but you get on with it. That is what you do in rugby.”

Erasmus has exercised his right to a full misconduct hearing after being handed the six-match ban.

title: New country welcomed into World Rugby fold as Oceania Rugby suspended
article_text:
Mali has been granted full World Rugby membership, while Oceania Rugby has been suspended from World Rugby Council membership pending an investigation into governance matters.

The decisions were among a series of outcomes announced following a World Rugby Council meeting in Dublin.

Mali’s application for full membership was unanimously approved by Council after a review process, completing a journey that began when the Malian Rugby Federation joined World Rugby as an associate member in 2004.

The promotion means Mali becomes World Rugby’s newest full member.

It takes the governing body’s total membership to 119 full members and 16 associate members.

World Rugby chair Brett Robinson said the decision reflected the progress made by the Malian Rugby Federation in developing and governing the game.

“Having been part of the World Rugby family since 2004, Mali’s progression to full membership represents an important step in the continued development of rugby in the country,” Robinson said.

Mali’s admission comes as World Rugby continues efforts to expand the game in emerging rugby markets, particularly across Africa. The federation has worked alongside Rugby Africa to grow participation and infrastructure within the country and has outlined ambitions to host major continental tournaments in the future.

The Council meeting also confirmed the reinstatement of Asia Rugby as a member of Council after meeting governance and administrative requirements.

Robinson said: “We are delighted to welcome back Asia Rugby, and their representatives Ada and Qais to Council, and look forward to working together to build a strong future for a region that will be represented by two nations – Japan and Hong Kong China – at a men’s Rugby World Cup for the first time next year. This will provide huge impetus for growth.”

Meanwhile, Oceania Rugby has been suspended from World Rugby Council membership while an investigation into governance matters takes place.

World Rugby stated that Oceania Rugby remains a member of the international federation and is cooperating fully with the process. Oceania Rugby is one of six regional associations of World Rugby, with 17 full member unions including the likes of Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, Samoa, and Tonga, as well as host of smaller Pacific island nations.

Samoa Rugby also remains self-suspended from Council membership while an ongoing review continues.

Further governance changes were confirmed with former Australia captain John Eales and ex-Argentina scrum-half Agustín Pichot elected to the World Rugby Executive Board as southern hemisphere high-performance union representatives.

The pair secured the highest number of votes from a ballot of 49 available votes and will replace SA Rugby president Mark Alexander and New Zealand representative Bart Campbell.

Under governance reforms approved in 2024, the Executive Board includes two northern hemisphere and two southern hemisphere high-performance union representatives alongside regional, performance, player and independent representatives.

Eales and Pichot take up their positions as World Rugby continues the rollout of its long-term strategic plan, which has included the introduction of new international competitions and a revised governance structure.

They succeed SA Rugby President Mark Alexander and New Zealand representative Bart Campbell.

“Congratulations to John and Agustín on their election to the Board,” said Robinson. “We are a year into implementation of our bold and ambitious new strategy, and John and Agustín will bring a new perspective and important insights as we continue to focus on making the business of rugby stronger, more resilient and impactful, while ensuring a game that is attractive and protects and supports our players on and off the field.”

title: Townsend makes 11 changes to Scotland side for Japan clash
article_text:
Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend has made 11 changes to the side that will face Japan in the Nations Championship on Saturday.

Only Zander Fagerson and captain Rory Darge, plus Darcy Graham and Tom Jordan - who shifts to fly-half - are retained in the starting line-up from the win over Australia last weekend.

Ollie Smith and Rory Hutchinson are involved for the first time and start at fullback and inside centre, with Stafford McDowall also handed a first start of the autumn at outside centre.

Kyle Rowe, who started the defeat to New Zealand, returns on the wing, alongside record try-scorer Graham, as Jamie Dobie starts at scrum-half.

Up front, Fagerson is joined by his Glasgow Warriors colleagues Nathan McBeth and Gregor Hiddleston, while Jonny Gray and Max Williamson form the second row partnership.

Liam McConnell has been handed a start at blindside flanker, while Ollie Leatherbarrow gets his first start after making his debut last weekend.

On the bench, Seb Stephen and Magnus Bradbury are set for their first involvements of the series with George Horne and Blair Kinghorn covering the back division on a 6:2 split.

title: Furbank leads returning England trio for All Blacks visit
article_text:
England have been boosted by the recovery and return of George Furbank, Seb Atkinson and Ollie Chessum to their starting line-up to face New Zealand on Saturday in the Nations Championship.

The trio, who all missed last weekend's win over Japan with knocks, are joined in the starting line-up by Will Joseph, who crossed for five tries against the Brave Blossoms.

Furbank held off the challenge of Freddie Steward, who impressed against Japan, to regain the full-back slot, while vice-captain Chessum brings ballast to a back row that is completed by Ben Curry and Ben Earl.

Fin Smith returns at fly-half to reprise a 10-12 combination with Atkinson that has started six of England's last seven Tests and dates back to their days as teenagers in Worcester Warriors academy.

Barring Joseph's inclusion for the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, England have named the same matchday 23 which combined excellently in the 45-12 victory over Australia a fortnight ago.

After last year's 33-19 success, England are aiming for successive wins over the All Blacks for the first time since beating them in November 2002 and June 2003 - five months before Rugby World Cup glory in Australia.

"There are few bigger occasions in international rugby than facing New Zealand," said head coach Steve Borthwick.

"It's a fixture that always carries a special significance, and one that the players are hugely looking forward to.

"We know the quality New Zealand have in their team. We've prepared for the very best version of them, knowing the challenge they will bring and the level we'll need to reach to get the result we want."

New Zealand, meanwhile, have also been bolstered by the return of big names.

Following their shock defeat by Wales in Cardiff last weekend, Jordie Barrett, Damian McKenzie and Cam Roigard are brought back in, while wing Will Jordan - his country's leading all-time try-scorer - has recovered from a hamstring issue to start.

Full-back Beauden Barrett, who skippered the side for the first time in Cardiff, will win his 150th Test cap, becoming only the fourth men's player - alongside Alun Wyn Jones, James Slipper and Sam Whitelock - to achieve the landmark.

Beauden and Jordie Barrett's brother Scott is in the second row, while Codie Taylor captains from hooker.

New Zealand lead the Nations Championship southern hemisphere standings by one point and any sort of victory over England is likely to be enough to book their place in the headline fixture of next weekend's play-off finals.

France, who lead the northern hemisphere table and play Argentina later on Saturday, would be their likeliest opponents.

A victory for England, however, could mean Borthwick's men forcing their way into the title play-off, while Ireland and South Africa, who meet in Dublin at 16:40 GMT, could also have a say in an intriguing finale to the group stage.

title: Ireland hooker Sheehan at number eight for Springboks game
article_text:
Ireland captain Dan Sheehan has been named at number eight for Saturday's highly anticipated Nations Championship match against world champions South Africa in Dublin.

Having won all 42 of his previous caps at hooker, the 28-year-old returns after recovering from a concussion to partner flankers Ryan Baird and Josh van der Flier in the back row.

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell has faced an injury crisis at number eight with regular skipper Caelan Doris, Jack Conan, Sean Jansen and recent debutant James McNabney all ruled out.

Nick Timoney, who was handed the jersey for last week's victory over Fiji, drops to the bench.

With Doris and Conan unavailable, Sheehan anchored the scrum in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster last month, but Saturday will be his first Test run-out in the back row.

"Most people would agree that he [Sheehan]'s a world-class player, not just good," said Farrell, who did not wish to comment on South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus' six-match ban for questioning the integrity of match officials.

"Throwing the ball in or scrummaging, his point of difference is in and around the field and how he plays the game with ball in hand or defensively, running lines and all of that.

"That's suited to number eight. He was training there all last week because he was on the 12-day return-to-play protocols, so we had a bit of a head start there, and he played there recently.

"He's very cool, calm and collected; there's no arrogance there whatsoever. Things don't bother him, so he takes it all in his stride, fully confident in his own ability."

Sheehan's move means that Ronan Kelleher keeps his place at hooker after starting the Fiji game, again joining props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong in the front row.

After being rested last week, Joe McCarthy returns to the second row to partner Tadhg Beirne, with Van der Flier edging out Timoney for the number seven jersey.

Sam Prendergast starts at fly-half after being cleared to face the Springboks on Wednesday, with Jamison Gibson-Park retained at scrum-half.

Prendergast, 23, was cited for his hip-drop tackle on Fiji's Peceli Yato - which was not punished on the pitch - but an independent disciplinary panel ruled the challenge was not worthy of a red card.

"Nothing's changed for us all week," Farrell said when asked about the possibility of a Prendergast ban.

"There's always something going on, whether it's dealing with HIA (head injury assessment) injuries or incidents like we've had with Sam this week.

"It (the hearing) was late on Tuesday night; we trained Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday and Sam's done all of that so there's been no hiccups for us, let's say that."

Robbie Henshaw and Stuart McCloskey both return to midfield after Farrell opted to pair Jamie Osborne and Bundee Aki in a new-look centre partnership against Fiji.

However, Osborne was replaced by McCloskey in the third minute after sustaining a pectoral injury that has ruled him out of the South Africa game, while Aki drops to the bench.

With Hugo Keenan returning to full-back for his 50th cap after sitting out the Fiji game, Mack Hansen switches to the left wing with Robert Baloucoune retained on the right. Tommy O'Brien, who scored two tries from the left wing against Fiji, drops out of the squad.

Farrell has opted for a split of five forwards and three backs on the bench. Tom Stewart, Tom O'Toole, Sam Illo, James Ryan and Timoney provide pack cover with Craig Casey, Ciaran Frawley and Aki named as backline reinforcements.

South Africa, who named their team on Monday, make five changes with record cap holder Eben Etzebeth recalled to the second row.

Cameron Hanekom is named at number eight, replacing Jasper Wiese, who was handed a four-week suspension after being sent off for a dangerous clear-out in last week's defeat by France.

Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw are named as the starting front row.

Erasmus also named Nche, Marx and Louw to start the France game but swapped them out for Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit shortly before kick-off at the Stade de France.

As part of the six-game ban handed down by World Rugby on Tuesday, Erasmus is not permitted to attend the Aviva Stadium encounter.

The 54-year-old has since announced he will be hosting an online watchalong of the match while he watches from his team's Dublin hotel.

South Africa sit second in the Nations Championship southern hemisphere standings, a point adrift of New Zealand.

A South Africa win over Ireland coupled with England beating the All Blacks (Saturday, 14:10 GMT) would be enough for Erasmus' side to seal a place in the 29 November final against the top-ranked northern hemisphere side at Twickenham.

Ireland must beat the Springboks and hope France and England falter against Argentina and New Zealand to finish top.

The Springboks won 24-13 at Aviva Stadium last year, their first victory over Ireland in Dublin since 2012.

Ireland: H Keenan; R Baloucoune, R Henshaw, S McCloskey, M Hansen; S Prendergast, J Gibson-Park; A Porter, R Kelleher, T Furlong, J McCarthy, T Beirne, R Baird, J van der Flier, D Sheehan (capt).

Replacements: T Stewart, T O'Toole, S Illo, J Ryan, N Timoney, C Casey, C Frawley, B Aki.

South Africa: Willemse; Arendse, Kriel, De Allende, Hooker; Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Van den Berg; Nche, Marx, Louw, Etzebeth, Nortje, Kolisi (capt), PS du Toit, Hanekom.

title: Scotland make 11 changes for Japan with yet another Lion forced to withdraw
article_text:
Scotland have retained just four starters from their victory over Australia as Gregor Townsend makes 11 changes for Saturday’s Nations Championship meeting with Japan at Scottish Gas Murrayfield.

Among those coming in is Newcastle Red Bulls back-row Ollie Leatherbarrow, who will make his first Test start at No.8 after making his debut from the bench in last weekend’s 15-12 victory over the Wallabies.

Darcy Graham, Tom Jordan, Zander Fagerson and captain Rory Darge are the only survivors from the XV that started against Australia, while British & Irish Lion Pierre Schoeman has become the latest player forced to withdraw through injury.

The loosehead has picked up a neck problem and has been replaced in the wider squad by Alec Hepburn. Schoeman joins fellow 2025 Lions Sione Tuipulotu, Ben White and Scott Cummings on the sidelines, with the trio already ruled out for the remainder of the Nations Championship earlier this week.

Leatherbarrow is joined in the back-row by Liam McConnell at blindside and Darge at openside, with the latter retaining the captaincy after his Player of the Match display against Australia.

Jonny Gray and Max Williamson form a new second-row pairing, while Nathan McBeth and Gregor Hiddleston come into the front row alongside Fagerson.

Jordan switches from inside centre to fly-half, with Jamie Dobie promoted from the bench to start at scrum-half. Stafford McDowall and Rory Hutchinson form a new midfield partnership.

Ollie Smith is named at full-back, with Graham moving to the right wing and Kyle Rowe coming in on the left.

Scotland have retained a six-two split among the replacements, where Seb Stephen and Magnus Bradbury could make their first appearances of the November campaign.

Scotland XV: 15 Ollie Smith, 14 Darcy Graham, 13 Stafford McDowall (vc), 12 Rory Hutchinson, 11 Kyle Rowe, 10 Tom Jordan, 9 Jamie Dobie, 1 Nathan McBeth, 2 Gregor Hiddleston, 3 Zander Fagerson, 4 Jonny Gray, 5 Max Williamson, 6 Liam McConnell, 7 Rory Darge (c), 8 Ollie Leatherbarrow.

Replacements: 16 Seb Stephen, 17 Rory Sutherland, 18 Will Hurd, 19 Gregor Brown, 20 Magnus Bradbury, 21 Matt Fagerson, 22 George Horne, 23 Blair Kinghorn.

title: Beauden Barrett to win 150th cap as All Blacks ring changes for England clash
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Beauden Barrett will make his 150th appearance for New Zealand as Dave Rennie brings back the big guns as the All Blacks look to bounce back against England.

Barrett captained the side in the shock defeat to Wales last week but retains his place at full-back in a heavily-changed backline, with younger brother Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan both passed fit to start.

Cam Roigard and Damian McKenzie return in the halves while Anton Lienert-Brown retains a starting spot following injury to Quinn Tupaea.

Up front, Codie Taylor captains the side from hooker, while Fabian Holland and Tupou Vaa’i are significant additions to the starting pack.

“It’s a great occasion for Beauden and his family. To wear the All Black Test jersey 150 times is an amazing achievement and testament to the impact he has had on this team over the past 15 seasons,” Rennie said. “He is a top man whose contribution off-field has been equally as impressive.

“England are a quality side and playing them at Allianz Stadium is always a big challenge. With the Hillary Shield and play-off spots for the Nations Championship Finals weekend all on the line, there is plenty to play for.”

England beat New Zealand last November in a defeat that precipitated the departure of head coach Scott Robertson.

Rennie was brought in as a replacement earlier this year but is facing fresh pressure after a first defeat to Wales in 73 years.

The eldest Barrett brother becomes the second All Black, after Sam Whitelock, and fourth player overall to reach 150 Test caps.

New Zealand XV: 1 Ethan de Groot, 2 Codie Taylor (capt.), 3 Fletcher Newell; 4 Scott Barrett, 5 Fabian Holland; 6 Tupou Vaa’i, 7 Peter Lakai, 8 Wallace Sititi; 9 Cam Roigard, 10 Damian McKenzie; 11 Josh Moorby, 12 Jordie Barrett, 13 Anton Lienert-Brown, 14 Will Jordan; 15 Beauden Barrett.

Replacements: 16 Asafo Aumua, 17 George Bower, 18 Pasilio Tosi, 19 Anton Segner, 20 Leicester Fainga’anuku; 21 Cortez Ratima, 22 Richie Mo’unga, 23 Rieko Ioane.

title: Botham 'disappointed' to be rested after starring against All Blacks
article_text:
Wales took the decision to take James Botham out of the side to face Australia for rugby reasons rather than paternity leave.

The blind-side flanker was named man of the match when he helped Steve Tandy's side create history by beating New Zealand at Principality Stadium.

The 28-year-old Cardiff forward made 30 tackles and got through a mountain of work.

Botham's partner is expecting their first child this week, but that was not the reason for club-mate Alex Mann's return in his place.

"We are obviously aware of it [the pregnancy] and for James, regardless of whether he was playing or not, that would be the primary focus, but it wasn't something that was part of selection," said head coach Tandy.

Mann has started in 12 of 14 Tests under Tandy and returns along with number eight Aaron Wainwright, who missed the All Blacks game because of a leg injury.

Botham and his Cardiff team-mate Taine Basham drop out of the matchday squad, with promising Exeter flanker Kane James set to win his second cap off the bench.

"James is disappointed not to play, but we have some amazing young men in our group," said Tandy about Botham.

"In training on Tuesday he was leading the charge and doing Australia things.

"We know if we want to be consistent in the long term then we need everyone going in the right way and providing competition.

"We have made changes in the back row because we feel it's an energy piece, Manny and Waino are pretty good players as well.

"Waino missed out through injury last week and Taine [Basham] stepped up, Manny played really well against Japan and will add energy."

Back-row forward Taine Plumtree made a big impact as a replacement in the final quarter against New Zealand.

He remains on the bench for the Wallabies and will also cover lock in the absence of Adam Beard, who is likely to be available for Nations Championship finals weekend after a shoulder injury.

title: CHIMP SPORT: Lady Cranes Set Sights on SVNS 2 Promotion in Dubai
article_text:
Uganda’s national women’s rugby sevens team, the Lady Cranes, have been flagged off for the HSBC SVNS 3 tournament scheduled for November 27–28 in Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

The 15-member contingent, comprising 12 players and three officials, was flagged off on Thursday at Cooper Chimney in Lugogo ahead of the two-day competition at The Sevens Stadium.

Uganda earned qualification for the Dubai event after winning their maiden Rugby Africa Women’s Sevens tournament in Nairobi, Kenya, earlier this month.

The victory secured the Lady Cranes a direct place in the third tier of World Rugby’s revamped sevens competition structure, where six nations will battle for promotion to HSBC SVNS 2.

Uganda will face China, Colombia, Poland, Samoa and Mexico in a round-robin format, with the top two teams securing qualification for the next tier, scheduled for early 2027 in Nairobi, São Paulo and Montevideo.

Head coach Onencan Charles believes the team can build on its recent success in Nairobi despite the limited preparation time.

“We’ve prepared quite well. It has been a very short time since we returned from Nairobi for the Rugby Africa tournament, but the girls are geared up because we still have the momentum from the recent competition,” Onencan said.

Captain Peace Lekuru also expressed confidence in the team’s readiness, identifying a top-two finish as their primary target.

“Our main goal is to finish in the top two and qualify for HSBC SVNS 2. Everyone is focused and prepared for the competition ahead. I feel so excited to lead the team again,” Lekuru said.

Players: Peace Lekuru (Captain), Adong Susan, Mufuwa Racheal, Namabiro Lydia, Nayiga Sarah Kirabo, Namukwaya Fazirah, Nabaggala Grace, Akello Tina Molly, Namutebi Bushira, Namboozo Matsula, Namulala Unity and Nandawula Juliet.

Management: Onencan Charles (Head Coach), Winnie Atyang (Team Manager) and Mayeku Nelson (Team Physiotherapist).

title: Scotland suffer Pierre Schoeman injury blow as Alec Hepburn gets Japan chance
article_text:
Scotland have suffered an injury blow with prop Pierre Schoeman ruled out of the clash with Japan due to a neck problem.

The experienced Edinburgh loosehead has left the Scotland camp and returned to his club for further assessment, leaving Gregor Townsend without one of his key forwards.

Schoeman’s absence has, however, opened the door for Alec Hepburn to join the squad as Scotland prepare for their final assignment of the campaign.

Townsend’s side will be aiming to finish on a high against Japan and build on their victory over Australia, having previously suffered defeat against New Zealand.

Read more: Scottish Rugby on how finances have taken step forward despite £1.4m loss

A convincing win could also prove significant as Scotland battle for the best possible finish in the standings.

Scotland and Wales appear locked in a fight for fourth place, with points difference potentially crucial depending on results elsewhere.

Ireland remain capable of being dragged into the equation, although that would require an almighty pasting against the Springboks combined with either Scotland or Wales running riot in their respective fixtures.

For Scotland, the focus will be on taking care of their own business against Japan despite losing Schoeman from the pack.

title: Wainwright and Adams back for Wales against Australia
article_text:
Wales have made four changes to the side that made history against New Zealand for the Nations Championship fixture against Australia.

Head coach Steve Tandy has tinkered with the starting line-up that beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years at Principality Stadium.

Wales go with the same XV that opened the Nations Championship with a 28-21 victory against Japan.

Alex Mann comes in for James Botham at blind-side flanker, Aaron Wainwright is back from a leg injury at number eight, lock Ben Carter returns for the injured Adam Beard and Josh Adams gets the nod on the wing.

Botham was man of the match against New Zealand but is not included after a huge defensive effort.

His partner is expecting their first child this week, but Wales say that is not the reason for the flanker sitting out the Wallabies game.

Exeter flanker Kane James is set to win his second cap from the bench after making his debut against Argentina in July.

Scarlets centre or fly-half Joe Hawkins also comes in for Ospreys playmaker Dan Edwards, who suffered an ankle injury in training that has led to Cardiff's Jarrod Evans being called into the Nations Championship squad.

Taine Plumtree will cover the second row in the absence of Beard, who suffered a shoulder injury against New Zealand.

Number eight Taine Basham and wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb drop out of the matchday squad after starting against the All Blacks.

Tandy says he had always intended to make changes.

"We made nearly 350 tackles, the ball in play time was one of the highest in Test rugby in the last three years and we have got competition," said the Wales head coach.

"The plan was always to freshen up and we are likely to do similar for the week after, because we need to find out about players.

"We have fresh and hungry players coming in, which will add the energy that we need at the weekend.

"The training environment is getting more competitive in certain positions we have the ability to put people in and feel confident about performance."

Eleven players will have started all three Tests - eight from English clubs and the Scarlets trio of full-back Blair Murray, centre Eddie James and fly-half Sam Costelow.

Wing Adams will win his 75th cap and returns after being left out against New Zealand despite scoring twice against Japan.

The 31-year-old Cardiff back has shown no signs of disappointment according to Tandy, despite missing out on history.

"He is a class rugby player but also a class man," he said.

"He is a big leader and is over the moon for the group. You saw him driving standards on the Tuesday and he knows where we need to go and how we need to keep building.

"He is an incredible person and did really well against Japan, but we need to have competition, to grow and keep pushing."

After beating Japan and the All Blacks, Wales are looking to complete a Cardiff hat-trick against the Wallabies.

They then travel to Twickenham's Allianz Stadium for finals weekend when they will play a southern hemisphere opponent, which could well be another fixture against the Japanese.

Tandy said: "It's our last home game of this competition. The support that fans give to the players and staff has been incredible and we can't wait to get back out at Principality Stadium."

The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has stated it has already sold more than 60,000 tickets for the fixture at Principality Stadium, which holds just under 74,000.

That figure exceeds the 55,152 that witnessed history against the All Blacks, despite the late kick-off time against the Wallabies.

Exeter's Tom Hooper has been named in the second row for Australia while flanker Carlo Tizzano starts in five forward changes from the team that lost to Scotland.

The front rows rotate roles for this Test with Isaac Kailea, Brandon Paenga-Amosa and Taniela Tupou selected as the starting combination, with Angus Bell, Billy Pollard and Allan Alaalatoa the replacements.

Lock Jeremy Williams and Fraser McReight are also on the bench as Australia contend with a six-day turnaround.

Wallabies head coach Les Kiss said: "We know we need to step up against a Welsh team full of confidence and momentum after their historic win against the All Blacks last weekend.

"Pulling on the gold jersey against Wales at Principality Stadium in Cardiff creates one of the great atmospheres in world rugby and we are focused on being up for the occasion."

Wales: Murray; Rees-Zammit, E James, Llewellyn, Adams; Costelow, T Williams; Smith, Lake (capt), Griffin, Jenkins, Carter, Mann, Morgan, Wainwright.

Replacements: Elias, G Thomas, Lewis, Plumtree, K James, Morgan-Williams, Hawkins, Hennessey.

Replacements: Pollard, Bell, Alaalatoa, Williams, McReight, Thomas, Donaldson, Daugunu.

Assistant referees: Karl Dickson (England) & Jeremy Rozier (France).

title: Wales name team to face Australia as four come in and star to make home debut
article_text:
Wales have named their team to face Australia on Saturday, with Steve Tandy making four changes to the side that made history against New Zealand last week.

Last weekend’s starting XV wrote itself into Welsh rugby folklore by ending the 73-year wait for another win over the All Blacks. But that hasn’t stopped Tandy from making changes - with four new faces in his walk-on side for Saturday night.

It’s not a totally new combination - with Tandy reverting to the starting side that faced Japan at the start of the campaign.

In the backs, Josh Adams is brought back into the left wing - having been rested last week - with Gabriel Hamer-Webb missing out.

There’s three changes to the pack - with Aaron Wainwright back from injury to start at No. 8 ahead of Taine Basham.

Alex Mann replaces last week's player of the match James Botham in the back-row, while Ben Carter is in for Adam Beard.

On the bench, Kane James is set to win his first cap on home soil - having been named as a replacement.

Joe Hawkins is also in line for his first appearance of the autumn, being named on the bench - with Dan Edwards injured.

The Wallabies named their team for Saturday's match early on Thursday morning, with head coach Les Kiss making five changes to his pack.

"The focus this week has been on continuing to build and challenge our game in a short preparation week," said Kiss. “We know we need to step up against a Welsh team full of confidence and momentum after their historic win against the All Blacks last weekend.

“Pulling on the gold jersey against Wales at Principality Stadium in Cardiff creates one of the great atmospheres in world rugby and we are focused on being up for the occasion.”
