title: Jannik Sinner’s latest decision sparks concern as new injury update emerges
article_text:
It is unclear when Jannik Sinner will return from the right knee injury that has sidelined him since July, and a new update has now emerged.

Sinner has not played since he defeated Alexander Zverev in the 2026 Wimbledon final to defend his title at the grass-court major.

While Sinner has not shared details about the specific nature of his knee injury, Sky Sport Italy have reported that the issue he is dealing with is iliotibial band syndrome (ITBS).

Last week, Sinner divulged he is hoping to make his comeback before the 2027 Australian Open.

“The goal is to go to Australia; I hope to get there, and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand,” said the world No 2.

“Right now, I need to follow the protocols without rushing things. I have a lot of faith in the process, and I’m working toward that objective.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

“Initially, we had an impossible goal for my return in mind, so we took a different path. I’m a tennis player, not a doctor, so my only option is to trust them.

“I miss playing tennis. Right now, however, it is crucial that I take care of my body, because I want to keep playing for another 10 to 15 years.”

The 25-year-old Italian added: “I’m fine. We’re doing everything we can — and more — to get back on the court as soon as possible.

“I have a great team with many experts to help us come back stronger.”

Vanity Fair Italia has reported Sinner is set to fly to America “to consult another specialist and determine the best course of action to return to the field without risking a relapse.”

The report added: “After meeting with Professor Alberto Zangrillo and a team from the San Raffaele Hospital in Milan, Jannik wants a further opinion before making any decisions.”

The revelation that Sinner will speak to another specialist has sparked some concern among fans about the condition of his knee.

It seems far from certain that the five-time Grand Slam champion will be fit for the start of the 2027 season.

title: ATP Finals 2026: Draw and schedule as Carlos Alcaraz, Alexander Zverev qualify for semifinals
ATP Finals: Ben Shelton beats Rafael Jodar to move within touching distance of semi-finals
article_text:
Ben Shelton battled past Rafael Jodar to move within touching distance of a place in the ATP Finals last four.

US Open runner-up Shelton only lost his serve once but still had to fight for just over two hours to beat the fast-rising Spaniard 7-6 (10-8) 7-5.

American Shelton closed out the match with three aces in a row and then wrote "I'll be watching, Arthur" on the camera lens - a reference to the final game in the group.

Shelton will progress to the semi-finals if world number one Alexander Zverev beats France's Arthur Fils later on Thursday.

Fils would need to beat Zverev in straight sets if he is to qualify instead of Shelton.

"I think if he takes Sascha [Zverev] out in straights, I'll say too good and go on holidays," Shelton joked of his good friend Fils.

"I'm always rooting for him [Arthur] and I think he and Sascha will have a great match.

"I'd love to make the semi-finals for the first time. I'll definitely be watching."

Germany's Zverev, unbeaten so far at the season-ending event, is assured of top place in the John McEnroe Group, and will play either Daniil Medvedev or Frances Tiafoe in Saturday's semi-finals.

Shelton did not win a match on his ATP Finals debut last year, but arrived in Turin with a Masters 1000 title and a first Grand Slam final under his belt.

He beat Fils in three entertaining sets in his opening match before being swept aside by Zverev on Tuesday.

Shelton was under pressure against Jodar in the first set, saving two break points and missing a series of routine shots when his opponent was struggling.

However, after taking a tight tie-break, Shelton quickly broke to take control of the third set.

Jodar, competing in his first professional season on the ATP Tour, was strong defensively and wrestled the break back to level at 4-4.

However, he was visibly fatigued and unable to keep Shelton at bay in a series of lengthy rallies, with Shelton breaking for 6-5.

Shelton slipped at the back of court as he served for the match, but recovered quickly to close out victory. He finished with 14 aces to one double fault, having dropped only 11 points behind his first serve.

In the doubles, Britain's Henry Patten and Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara will need to beat French pair Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti if they are to keep their title defence alive.

Wimbledon champions Patten and Heliovaara have won one and lost one of their three group matches.

title: WTA names Jamie Baker chief tour officer
article_text:
- Former British No. 2 and Wimbledon Tournament Director brings extensive experience across professional tennis, tournament operations and player relations

The WTA (Women's Tennis Association) on Thursday announced the appointment of Jamie Baker as Chief Tour Officer. A former professional player and most recently Associate Director of Professional Tennis and Tournament Director at Wimbledon, Baker brings a distinctive combination of experience as a competitor, tournament leader, and business professional to the WTA. He will join the organization during the first quarter of 2027.

In his new role, Baker will oversee Tour operations, player and tournament relations, and performance health, working closely with players, tournaments, and colleagues across the organization. His appointment adds significant tennis and operational expertise to the WTA's leadership team as the organization builds on its recent success delivering the WTA Finals back in the U.S.

"Jamie brings an exceptional combination of experience as a professional player and a leader at one of the world's most prestigious tournaments," said Valerie Camillo, Chair and CEO of the WTA. "He understands the sport from multiple perspectives, from the player experience to the operational demands of running a major international event. His expertise and judgment will be invaluable as we continue to grow the Tour and deliver enhanced services to our players and tournaments."

"Jamie has a deep understanding of what it takes to deliver professional tennis at the highest level, and he brings a valuable perspective on the needs of players and tournaments," said Adam Barrett, WTA Tournament Council Chair and Tournament Board Representative. "His experience and collaborative approach will be an asset to the WTA and to the broader tennis community. We look forward to working with him in this new role."

"I'm delighted to be joining the WTA at such an important moment of opportunity. The WTA has an extraordinary legacy and has played a defining role in shaping the future of women's sport. As women's sports continue to grow and attract new audiences and investment, the WTA is uniquely positioned to help lead that next chapter, drawing on its rich history, its athletes, and the global reach of the sport. I'm honored to be part of that work and look forward to contributing to the future of the Tour," said Baker.

Baker joins the WTA from The All England Lawn Tennis Club (AELTC), where he served as Associate Director of Professional Tennis and Tournament Director. In that role, he led tennis matters for The Championships, overseeing key aspects of tournament operations, including officiating, scheduling, player services, and practice facilities. He was also responsible for the player experience, grass court strategy, and relationships with the ATP, WTA, and World Tennis.

His experience at Wimbledon follows a career that spans both sides of professional tennis. Prior to tournament leadership, Baker competed on the ATP Tour, where he was ranked as high as British No. 2 before retiring from professional tennis in 2013.

Following his playing career, Baker spent nearly five years in corporate banking at Santander before joining The AELTC as Head of Tennis Relations in 2018. He was promoted to Head of Professional Tennis and Tournament Director in 2020 and became Associate Director of Professional Tennis in 2024.

At the WTA, Baker will bring this combination of competitive, operational, and business experience to the work of supporting players and tournaments and managing the Tour. His experience managing a world-class tournament will be instrumental in the WTA's new approach to self-operating the WTA Finals and the work to build out the event in Charlotte.

With the addition of the Chief Tour Officer role, Valerie Camillo will be CEO of the WTA in addition to her role as Chair. Camillo will partner with Marina Storti in her role as CEO of WTA Ventures, the commercial arm of the WTA.

title: American tennis player receives two-year ban after testing positive for same substance as Jannik Sinner
article_text:
Jessica Eudovic has been handed a two-year ban by the International Tennis Intregrity Agency after testing positive for clostebol in the 2025 season.

The star had been provisionally suspended for over a year since testing positive at a World Tennis Tour event in Santa Tecla, El Salvador, on the 1st October 2025.

The process was drawn out due to Eudovic challenging the suspension, which caused the case to be moved to a independent tribunal.

Following a two-day hearing in October, Eudovic has still received the ban, which she will now need to serve a year of after already missing 12 months of action.

According to the ITIA, “the tribunal found that while Eudovic did not establish how clostebol entered her system, the breach was not intentional.

“In reaching its decision, the tribunal considered the scientific evidence, including the very low level of clostebol detected in Eudovic’s sample, the circumstances of the case, and Eudovic’s evidence.

“As Eudovic was unable to establish how the prohibited substance entered her system, despite accessing the ITIA’s support fund for product testing, the tribunal could not consider a further reduction of the sanction. Eudovic was therefore suspended for two years.

“Time served under provisional suspension is credited against the sanction. As such, Eudovic’s suspension ends on 20 November 2027. Eudovic’s results from the event in Santa Tecla are also disqualified, with the associated ranking points and prize money forfeited.

“While suspended, Eudovic is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.”

This is, of course, not the first time a player has tested positive for clostebol, which is banned synthetic anabolic–androgenic steroid.

Jannik Sinner is perhaps the most high-profile player to receive a ban after testing positive for clostebol, as he missed three months of action after a settlement with the International Tennis Integrity Agency.

Lower down the tennis rankings, and the likes of Karlis Ozolins and Daniil Kakhniuk have also been suspended due to testing positive for clostebol.

As for Eudovic, the star’s early career has been rocked by the case and the suspension.

She has not played competitively since appearing at a WTT W35 tournament in Boca Raton, United States in November of last year.

By the time she will return to action she will be 20 years old, so there is plenty of time for her to hit the ground running and bounce back from the ban.

She has been ranked as high as world No 1104 in the rankings.

title: Iconic tennis tournament faces being axed and two more replaced at crunch ATP meeting
article_text:
An iconic tournament on the ATP Tour is at risk of being axed, with two more also on the chopping block, as per reports. It comes as the Tour's chiefs meet in Turin at the end of the 2026 tennis season.

And on the table at that crunch meeting, according to Cor Sport, is the future of the Mexican Open. The tournament, which has been held in Acapulco since 2001, is potentially getting the chop from the 2028 season onwards.

Meanwhile, the other two at-risk tournaments are Doha and Dubai, with talk that they could be scrapped from the schedule as early as 2027. That's due to ongoing unrest in the Middle East, with tournaments in the region disrupted earlier this year.

The leadership at the ATP are said to be deep in discussions about how to handle the geopolitical crisis, with suggestions that the two ATP 500 events could be moved or even replaced. The governing body is wary of mid-season disruption again and therefore wants to act with foresight.

The two tournaments are currently scheduled for February, with Doha taking place the week before the tour rolls into Dubai. There has been a suggestion that the Tour is keen for one ATP 500 event to host two tournaments in consecutive weeks. But both Rotterdam and Dallas and Delray Beach have already communicated their inability to do this.

By contrast, organisers in Rio de Janeiro have proposed a back-to-back tournament in Brazil, but the drawback is that it would be on clay. The ATP isn't convinced by that proposal and therefore it's been mooted that they could just create a brand new tournament in a location that is yet to be decided.

There is talk that Rio, along with Gstaad, Kitzbuhel, Umago and Bastad could all switch to hard courts. However, that wouldn't happen until 2029 at the earliest. Also on the agenda was a discussion about the distribution of ranking points and the future of doubles on tour.

On court, the season-ending ATP Finals are ongoing, with top two seeds Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz both qualified for the semi-finals.

title: Alcaraz undergoes MRI on hamstring and cancels training, his ATP Finals in the balance (report)
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz had scans on his left hamstring and right knee in Turin around midday and called off his 1 pm training session. With no result released, Friday’s dead rubber against Cobolli and Saturday’s semi-final now hang on his condition.

Carlos Alcaraz had an MRI scan on his left hamstring and his right knee around midday on Thursday in Turin, then pulled out of his training session. It comes a day after he needed treatment during his 6-2, 6-4 win over Daniil Medvedev. The result had not been made public at the time of writing, and neither the ATP nor his team has made a statement.

The scan took place at the Istituto di Medicina dello Sport, close to the Inalpi Arena, according to Sky Sport Italia and EFE. Sky Sport Italia says he arrived at 12:08 and left at around 1:15 pm. He was accompanied by his doctor Juanjo López, his physio Juanjo Moreno and his fitness coach Alberto Lledó, according to El Español.

His training session, planned for 1 pm with the Brazilian junior Guto Miguel, was cancelled. He was taken off the schedule a minute before it was due to start, according to EFE, as a precaution. A first check on Wednesday evening had shown nothing conclusive, the injury being too recent.

On Wednesday, Alcaraz had played the problem down without closing the door. “I feel it a little bit. I’m not gonna lie,” he said in his press conference. “Right now I’m just feeling okay.” He added: “We will see with my team, with my physio, but I think the rest of the day and tomorrow is really going to be important days ahead of me.”

He had already secured first place in Group Lendl that evening, when Frances Tiafoe beat Flavio Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0. The right knee is not a new subject: he had already been protecting it in training before the tournament.

Alcaraz is due to face Cobolli on Friday, at 2 pm according to the Spanish press, in a match with nothing at stake in the standings: Alcaraz is first and Cobolli is eliminated. For Alcaraz, though, the rule makes it decisive. A player who withdraws from a round-robin match after the first round cannot play the knockout stage, so if he does not play Cobolli, he is out.

If he starts the match and retires, he can still play Saturday’s semi-final against the runner-up of the McEnroe Group, subject to a favourable medical opinion, according to Sky Sport Italia and EFE. His replacement would be Alex de Minaur, the first alternate according to the Italian press (Sky Sport Italia, Adnkronos).

The Davis Cup is also in view. Alcaraz is in Spain’s team for the Final 8 in Bologna, from 24 to 29 November, with a quarter-final against Austria on 26 November according to Sky Sport Italia. There is a precedent: in 2025, after losing the ATP Finals final to Jannik Sinner, an oedema of the right hamstring, detected on MRI, kept him out of the Davis Cup. His withdrawal was announced on 18 November 2025.

His Davis Cup teammate Rafael Jodar, speaking in Spanish after his defeat to Ben Shelton on Thursday, said he has not yet spoken to Alcaraz. “I haven’t had time to talk to either Carlos or the captain yet,” he said. “I see Carlos very motivated to play this competition and to give everything for his country.” He added: “If he is physically and mentally well, which I believe is the case, he will be with us, but obviously it is a decision for his team and for him.”

title: Hong Kong Open: Teen Santhosh Ramraj Shocks Idol Chen
article_text:
Never meet your heroes, unless you are 19-year-old Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj, in which case you might just knock them out of a Super 500 tournament.

The Indian world No.47 delivered the shock of LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Thursday, toppling pre-tournament favourite and world No.4 Chen Yu Fei 21-18 24-22 in the second round.

Just 24 hours after banking her maiden top 20 scalp against Mia Blichfeldt, Santhosh Ramraj bagged her first top 10 victory – becoming the first player outside the top 30 to beat Chen since Gregoria Mariska Tunjung in 2017.

“She’s my biggest idol and I still can’t believe I won against her,” Santhosh Ramraj admitted afterward, visibly awestruck. “This will be one of the most memorable days in my playing career.”

The win was no fluke. Combining fearless aggression with stubborn defence, Santhosh Ramraj refused to blink even when staring down a 15-5 deficit in the second game. Ironically, her secret weapon was simply mentally clocking in for a decider.

“Actually, I was preparing for the third game,” she laughed. “I just didn’t want to give up so easily. Since she’s so senior, I had nothing to lose, so I kept on trying. It worked out really well that I was able to close the gap.”

Behind the giantkilling performance lies a quiet story of family sacrifice. Six years ago, her family uprooted their lives in Coimbatore and moved to Hyderabad so she could train at the Gopichand Academy – a leap of faith now paying dividends. Having reached the Korea Masters semifinals in August, she is now into her first Super 500 quarterfinal of the season.

“I think I’m not less than anyone,” she said, the awe quickly giving way to conviction. “I’m very thankful to all my coaches for supporting me throughout this journey.”

Her reward for slaying her idol? A maiden clash with Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong, who swept Lin Hsiang Ti 21-11 21-12 to keep her HSBC BWF World Tour Finals hopes alive.

If Thursday proved anything, Chochuwong shouldn’t expect the teenager to show too much respect.

title: Satwik-Chirag cruise into Hong Kong Open quarterfinals
article_text:
Hong Kong Open: Rakshitha Ramraj stuns world No.4 Chen Yufei to reach quarterfinals

Meanwhile, the fifth seed Satwik-Chirag beat the Malaysian pair in straight games to reach the men's doubles last eight.

Rakshitha Ramraj continued her impressive run as she stunned world No. 4 Chen Yufei to storm into the quarterfinals of the Hong Kong Open Super 500 on Thursday.

The 19-year-old Indian secured a straight-games victory (21-18, 24-22) over the former Olympic champion and five-time world medallist in 45 minutes.

“This is the biggest win of my career. She is my biggest idol, and I still can’t believe I beat her. This will be the most memorable day of my career,” Ramraj said in her post-match interview.

“I’m very happy that whatever I played worked out really well. My attack was really good today, and that was the key. I believe I can do even better in the future,” she added.

After taking the opening game, Ramraj produced a remarkable fightback in the second, recovering from 5-15 down to close it out 24-22, and setting up a quarterfinal clash with Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong.

“I was actually preparing for a third game, but I didn’t want to give up so easily. I kept trying, and in the end it worked really well to cover the deficit,” she said.

This is the biggest win of Ramraj’s career so far. She had earlier caused another upset in the first round by defeating world No. 20 Mia Blichfeldt of Denmark.

Meanwhile, Indian men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty also moved to the quarter-finals with a straight-game win over Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong.

The fifth-seeded Indians, who won two Super 750 titles this year at Singapore and China, put up a clinical show during their 21-19, 21-16 win over Nur and Tan in 42 minutes.

Satwik and Chirag will next face China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi on Friday, who beat Japan’s Kakeru Kumagai and Hiroki Nishi 21-19, 21-17.

Earlier, the Indian duo needed three games to get past Chinese Taipei’s Lee Jhe-Huei and Yang Po-Hsuan in the opening round.

In the women’s doubles, the world bronze medalists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand lost to the American pair of Lauren Lam and Allison Lee 20-22, 13-21 in the pre-quarterfinals to end their campaign.

Lakshya Sen, who has sealed his place in the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, also reached the last eight with a 21-11, 21-18 win over Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke in the men’s singles pre-quarterfinals.

title: ‘I see comments every day’: Sonay Kartal’s fightback against injury and online abuse
article_text:
Sonay Kartal believes the vitriolic abuse and threats that she and her fellow players receive after every match have become an unavoidable part of her job.

“Unfortunately, it’s something that comes with the sport,” the British No 2 says. “I don’t really have a choice to not deal with it. Obviously, it’s not a good thing to have and as a player, win or lose, you’re seeing those things.

“You can try and take yourself away from it as much as you can and you can do different things to your [social media] account to try and hide it, but it’s a shame that it is something we have to deal with and hopefully it can change. But we’ve all been there, we know what it’s like when you have a loss and you see your social media flooded with not very nice comments.”

Social media abuse has been a constant theme for players in recent years, particularly due to the prevalence of sports betting, and many have spoken out. Most recently, her compatriot Jodie Burrage reposted some of the barrage of abuse received on her Instagram account earlier this month.

While the governing bodies have developed some tools to monitor it, and limit the comments that players see, Kartal notes that most of those initiatives come at the cost of privacy, making them a less than ideal solution. “I see those comments every day, it’s hard to avoid them,” she says.

“You look at a post, you look at your Instagram, and they’re there. At the start, it was not very nice to read but unfortunately I’m used to it now so it’s just another one. You just deal with it. It is what it is.”

Kartal was speaking from the comfort of the National Tennis Centre, her home away from home, at the end of perhaps the most challenging season of her career. In March, she defeated the 2025 Australian Open champion, Madison Keys, to reach the last 16 at Indian Wells, an excellent result. At No 54 in the world rankings, she sat 10 spots away from her career-high No 44 and it seemed she would keep on moving forward. Instead, she would not compete for another six months after being diagnosed with a stress fracture in her back.

As she reflects on months of long rehab and the frustration of working through her injury at Roehampton while surrounded by players sweeping in and out between tournaments, Kartal describes the first month as the most painful. “It was just very uncomfortable,” she says. “I had a lot of nerve pain, too. I wouldn’t wish sciatica pain upon anyone. Back pain and nerve pain is not fun.

“I would just be doing normal things like brushing my teeth or putting my shoes on and I’m in quite a lot of pain, which is not fun. For a 24-year-old it was not something I really wanted to deal with, which is another reason why I just had to let this get better. I couldn’t really rush it because it’s six months of my time now versus maybe it’s post-Sonay’s tennis life constantly having back pain.”

Her response was spectacular. While some players naturally take time to find their timing or match instincts after such a long time out, Kartal hit the ground running immediately. In just her third tournament back at the Wuhan Open in October, she defeated Belinda Bencic, Jasmine Paolini, Elina Svitolina and Jelena Ostapenko, four former top-five players, consecutively to reach her first WTA 1000 final – and led Maja Chwalinska in the final before being beaten in three sets.

Having tumbled to No 170 in the world that week due to her extended absence, that result allowed her ranking to skyrocket, and she is now at No 53 as she prepares for the new season. She also briefly became the British No 1 – Katie Boulter has since leapfrogged her once more – for the first time.

Kartal’s next goal is to be seeded at the major tournaments and, having dragged herself so quickly back to where she was before the injury, to keep on pushing forward: “I didn’t worry about ever getting back to that level,” she says, shrugging. “I just wasn’t sure how long it would take me.”

Ash Barty and Shingo Kunieda to be Inducted Into International Tennis Hall of Fame
article_text:
Major moments inspired all-court conviction in Ashleigh Barty.

Former world No. 1 Barty brought her best in Grand Slam finals posting a 3-0 record in Slam showdowns winning six of the seven sets she played in those finals.

Now, the 30-year-old Barty will receive tennis ultimate honor: Induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

Barty and Shingo Kunieda, the most decorated men’s wheelchair tennis player in history, winning a record 28 Grand Slam singles titles and 50 major titles overall, form the International Tennis Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027, the Hall announced today.

The Class of 2027 will be inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame during Hall of Fame weekend August 26–28, 2027 in Newport, Rhode Island.

The Barty Party peaked in a homecoming crescendo in January of 2022 as the top-seeded Aussie’s 6-3, 7-6 win over feisty American Danielle Collins snapped a 44-year home singles drought at the Australian Open and captivated Aussies.

Barty’s triumph drew a peak viewership of 4.26 million TV viewers Down Under making it the most widely-viewed Australian Open women’s final in Australia in history.

“I’m so grateful. Tennis has given me everything and more,” Barty said. “In my career, I’ve been introduced and connect with so many amazing people around the world. And it’s also given me the opportunity to have some of my dreams after tennis: Starting a family…

One of the greatest sub 5’8″ servers in tennis history, Barty was a highly-skilled all-court player who excelled on all surfaces.

Barty owns three Grand Slam titles on three different surfaces: 2022 Australian Open on hard court, 2021 Wimbledon on grass and 2019 Roland Garros on clay. Barty’s 114 consecutive weeks as world No. 1 is fourth on the all-time list behind only Serena Williams and Steffi Graf (186 consecutive weeks apiece) and Martina Navratilova (156 consecutive weeks).

When Barty won the 2021 Wimbledon, she joined Ann Jones, Martina Hingis and Amelie Mauresmo as the fourth junior champion to raise the Rosewater Dish. Barty was such a gifted athlete she played two sports professionally: Cricket and tennis. Barty took the entire 2015 season off and played pro cricket for the Brisbane Heat during her time away from tennis.

“To be able to win Wimbledon which was my dream, my one true dream that I wanted in tennis, really changed my perspective,” Barty said when she announced her 2022 retirement. “I just had that gut feeling after Wimbledon. I had spoken to my team quite a lot about it and there was just a little part of me that wasn’t quite fulfilled.

“Then came the challenge of the Australian Open. That for me just feels like my perfect way to celebrate what an amazing journey my tennis career has been. As a person, this is what I want.”

Alexander Zverev notified of lawsuit by former partner in abuse case during middle of ATP Finals
article_text:
World No 1 Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals on Wednesday.

The latest legal case brought by the mother of Zverev's former partner alleges the tennis player violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her.

The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with French sports news outlet L'Equipe earlier this year that "it has been proven that the accusations were false" and "my innocence has been proven."

Zverev's Berlin-based lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, confirmed in a statement shared with The Associated Press that they were formally served with Patea's lawsuit on Wednesday.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit," Zverev's lawyers said. "If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion" protected by the German constitution.

They said there had been no breach of any contractual obligations.

Patea's lawyer, Michael Scheele, told The Associated Press that Zverev's claim over his innocence "triggered a veritable storm of criticism against our client."

He said the backlash was damaging to her business as an influencer and that she also felt her honour had been violated.

"Quite apart from the fact that Zverev's claim is false, he was not permitted to make any public statements whatsoever, in any form," he said. "Both Brenda Patea and Alexander Zverev had agreed to this in a settlement."

Patea is seeking that Zverev be ordered not to repeat such comments and that he be fined up to £208,484 €250,000 euros every time if he does.

Zverev faced a charge of causing bodily harm to Patea during an argument in Berlin in May 2020. He always denied any wrongdoing.

The case ended in a district court in Berlin in 2024 after the settlement. Zverev agreed to pay fines to the state and charitable organisations.

Zverev this month ascended to the No 1 ranking for the first time. He also won his first two Grand Slam titles this year and is competing this week at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Zverev has not commented on the lawsuit.

He previously denied abuse allegations from another former girlfriend, Olga Sharypova, who first made the accusations in 2020 and followed up in 2021 with a detailed account in a Slate.com article that was taken down because of a preliminary injunction issued by a German court. Slate said it stood by the article.

The allegations prompted the men's professional tennis tour, the ATP, to investigate her claims. It ended 15 months later, in January 2023, with the ATP saying there was "insufficient evidence" to substantiate the claims.

title: Alcaraz gives injury update at Nitto ATP Finals
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz made it two wins from two on Wednesday at this year’s Nitto ATP Finals but walked off court with heavy strapping on his left leg following his victory against Daniil Medvedev.

The Spaniard received treatment on his upper left leg from the tournament physio when leading by a break at 2-1 in the second set. The 23-year-old did not appear hindered by the issue, and afterward gave an update on his condition.

“I feel it a little bit,” Alcaraz said in his post-match press conference when asked about his left leg. “I'm not going to lie. But, you know, unfortunately I was playing great, and suddenly I felt a little problem of my hamstring. But just a little bit.

“I could play really good tennis since that moment until the end of the match. I was really focused on other things. I was trying to stay relaxed, to move not too aggressive, let's say. I'm thinking about being aggressive and thinking about my shots all the time. So right now, I'm just feeling okay. We will see with my team, with my physio, but I think the rest of the day and tomorrow is really going to be important days ahead of me.”

Alcaraz knows all too well how quickly an injury can change a player's perspective. The Spaniard spent more than four months sidelined earlier this year after sustaining a wrist injury at the ATP 500 event in Barcelona. The No. 3 player in the PIF ATP Rankings eventually returned at the US Open in August, reaching the quarter-finals.

Since then, Alcaraz has lifted trophies in Paris, Vienna and Tokyo to arrive in Turin in outstanding form. But the time away from the court also left him with a renewed appreciation for the opportunity to compete, a perspective that came into focus again after Wednesday's hamstring concern.

“The injury made me realise what's important, what's really important,” Alcaraz said. “It's not winning, it's not winning or losing finals of tournaments. It's just about playing tennis. That's what I realise, that it is a gift every time that I can step on the court and compete healthy.

“When you realise that, everything comes easier for me, because I enjoy and I don't feel stressful on a tennis court, or most of the time I don't feel stressful on a tennis court, which means I could face the problems in a different way. More calm, relaxed, and I'm thinking, ‘OK, I'm going to still try my best tennis, I'm going to still try what I have to do.’”

Alcaraz will face Flavio Cobolli in his final round-robin match in Turin. The 29-time tour-level titlist is aiming to lift the trophy at the prestigious year-end event for the first time this week.

Be part of the action this fortnight in Turin and sign up here to ATP Unlocked for exclusive coverage in the Nitto ATP Finals Hub.

title: Alcaraz explains the treatment he received during his match against Medvedev
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz received treatment on his upper left leg during his win over Daniil Medvedev at the ATP Finals. In his press conference, he said he felt a little problem in his hamstring and would assess it with his team and his physio.

Carlos Alcaraz played down any concern after receiving treatment during his 6-2, 6-4 win over Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Leading by a break at 2-1 in the second set, the Spaniard received treatment from the tournament physio on his upper left leg, according to the ATP. He did not look hindered afterwards and closed out the match without facing a single break point.

In his on-court interview after the match, Alcaraz acknowledged he had a small physical problem during the match. He said everyone could see he was still able to play good tennis, and that he kept moving well.

He explained he did not want to push his body to its limits or force anything. With a break in hand at that moment, he simply tried to protect his lead with his serve and to play relaxed, and said he was pleased with how he handled it. He added that he would now assess the problem with his team.

Before the tournament, Alcaraz had already been seen training in Turin with protection on his right knee.

The alert comes at a key moment. With two wins from two matches in Group Lendl, Alcaraz will qualify for the semi-finals if Frances Tiafoe wins a set against Flavio Cobolli on Wednesday evening. He faces Cobolli in his last group match on Friday. All the scenarios are in our article: all the qualification scenarios at the ATP Finals.

title: Alcaraz continues winning run despite injury concern
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz continued his sensational late-season form as he outclassed world number five Daniil Medvedev to all but confirm his progress at the ATP Finals.

But the 23-year-old Spaniard later said he had felt "a little problem" with his hamstring.

Alcaraz produced another sparkling display to control the contest throughout, despite ending the match with heavy strapping on his upper-left leg.

The issue did not disrupt the world number three, who led by a set and a break when he received treatment on the area, as he cruised to a 6-2 6-4 win in just 72 minutes.

"Right now I'm just feeling OK," Alcaraz said.

"We will see with my team and physio, but I think the rest of today and tomorrow are really going to be important days ahead of me."

It was an 11th consecutive victory for the seven-time major winner, following back-to-back titles at the Vienna Open and Paris Masters.

Alcaraz will qualify for the semi-finals before his last group match against Flavio Cobolli on Friday if Frances Tiafoe wins a set against the Italian later on Wednesday.

Asked what pleased him most about his performance, Alcaraz replied: "Everything".

"We could see in [Medvedev's] first match that he was serving very well. I returned really well, really aggressively, and really deep," he added.

"I think I just hit the ball in a sweet spot every time. I'm really happy about it."

Given the outstanding levels at which he is currently operating, it is easy to forget that Alcaraz spent four months out of action in the middle of the season.

The former world number one's rapid return from that wrist injury to his scintillating best has been astonishing.

Alcaraz has won three titles and lost just twice in 24 matches since making his return at the US Open in August, when his lack of match fitness appeared to catch up with him in a four-and-a-half hour epic against Ben Shelton.

Just 10 weeks on, he delivered one of the best indoor performances of his career in sweeping past 2020 champion Medvedev.

That came two days after he began his latest bid for a first ATP Finals title with a statement victory over Tiafoe - and later warned his rivals he has never felt better at this stage of the season.

Medvedev beat home hope Cobolli in straight sets in his opening match for his first win against a top-10 opponent since defeating Alcaraz at Indian Wells in March.

The Russian was no match for the Australian Open champion on this occasion, however.

A dominant seven-game streak ultimately decided the match, as Alcaraz ran away with the first set and then broke immediately in the second to take firm control.

The second seed did not face a single break point as he outmanoeuvred Medvedev, firing 16 winners and committing just 13 unforced errors.

It was a display which scored 9.5 out of 10 on the ATP's performance rating, which combines several statistics to measure a player's overall game, following a 9.6 in his opener.

That was despite Alcaraz playing the final seven games with the issue in his hamstring, which he will now work to overcome in the next 48 hours.

title: Hong Kong Open: Kidambi Plays Kingmaker
article_text:
Kidambi Srikanth played ultimate kingmaker at LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Wednesday, pulling off a 21-16 16-21 21-9 surprise over Koki Watanabe to officially conclude the men’s singles Race to Finals.

Depending on results this week, a deep run from Watanabe could have denied Kidambi’s compatriot Lakshya Sen, Chou Tien Chen or Kunlavut Vitidsarn a coveted ticket to Hangzhou. Instead, Kidambi intervened – sealing victory in 51 minutes to avenge a straight-games loss to the Japanese shuttler just last week at the Kumamoto Masters.

The win came as a relief for Chou in particular, who had suffered a 19-21 21-7 21-19 defeat to rising Indonesian Moh Zaki Ubaidillah moments earlier. Sen had also survived a heart-stopping battle with Frenchman Arnaud Merkle 14- 21 21-16 25-23 while Vitidsarn beat Shogo Ogawa 21-7 23-21.

While Kidambi closed the door on the men’s singles race, several players in other disciplines kept their own HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 hopes alive by clearing their opening hurdles.

In mixed doubles, Sapsiree Taerattanachai and Pakkapon Teeraratsakul wasted little time dispatching Canadian duo Jonathan Lai/Crystal Lai 21-13 21-12. With compatriots Dechapol Puavaranukroh and Supissara Paewsampran still in the race despite a 21-18 21-13 loss to Dejan Ferdinansyah/Felisha Alberta Nathaniel Pasaribu, the regional traffic jam has become intense.

The Thais are now locked in a tense five-way tussle alongside tandems from neighbouring Malaysia – Goh Soon Huat/Shevon Jemie Lai and Hoo Pang Ron/Lai Pei Jing – plus Japan’s Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi, all of whom also advanced on Wednesday.

“We just try our best and keep winning as much as we can,” said Taerattanachai, acknowledging her fate is not entirely in her hands. “We know we can still make the cut but we must pray for our rivals to lose. All we can do is keep going until the end.”

Meanwhile, in women’s singles, Putri Kusuma Wardani is fighting to secure back-to-back Finals appearances after making her debut last year. Facing Letshanaa Karupathevan, Wardani overcame a first-game wobble to triumph 21-15 21-12.

Her path to qualification remains a dogfight against Thai contenders Ratchanok Intanon and Pornpawee Chochuwong, who both kept pace in the first round – Chochuwong outclassing Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt 21-11 21-11 and Intanon cruising past Peng Yu Wei 21-17 21-12.

As the final qualifying event, the stakes at the Kai Tak Arena couldn’t be higher, yet 2024 Hong Kong Open runner-up Wardani is choosing freedom over fear.

“Since this is the last World Tour tournament counting towards Hangzhou and the fact I had a good result here, there’s a bit of pressure,” she admitted. “But I don’t want to think too far ahead; just play with a ‘nothing to lose’ mindset every match.”

title: Lakshya Sen qualifies for BWF World Tour Finals after Watanabe's exit
article_text:
Kidambi Srikanth's win over Koki Watanabe confirms Lakshya's second appearance at the season-ending event in Hangzhou, where PV Sindhu will also compete.

India's Lakshya Sen sealed his place in the BWF World Tour Finals after compatriot Kidambi Srikanth knocked out his closest rival, Japan’s Koki Watanabe, in the men's singles first round of the Hong Kong Open Super 500 badminton tournament here on Wednesday.

With back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters Japan, Lakshya had come out of nowhere to climb to sixth spot in the World Tour rankings but his spot was not sealed, as Watanabe and Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn were also in the race to break into the top-eight and secure a place in the season finale in December.

On Wednesday, Srikanth beat Watanabe 21-16, 16-21, 21-9, ending the Japanese player’s hopes of making the season-ending event in Hangzhou, China, from December 9 to 13.

It was after Lakshya had survived a scare against Frenchman Arnaud Merkle, coming back from a game down to win 14-21, 21-16, 25-23 and enter the pre-quarterfinals.

Lakshya, with 74,180 points, and Watanabe, on 73,620, had been locked in a tight battle for one of the final spots in the HSBC Race to Finals standings. The Hong Kong Open is the last qualifying event of the season.

With Watanabe needing to beat Srikanth to stay in contention, his defeat meant he would no longer overtake Lakshya.

Vitidsarn and Chinese Taipei’s Chou Tien Chen have also secured their places in the BWF World Tour Finals following Watanabe’s exit.

This will be Lakshya’s second appearance at the World Tour Finals, having reached the semifinals on debut in 2021.

He is the second Indian to qualify for this year’s edition after PV Sindhu, who made the cut in the women’s singles.

Lakshya will next face Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke in the pre-quarterfinals on Thursday. Srikanth will take on Korea’s Yoo Tae Bin.

It was also a good day for Rakshitha Ramraj as she recorded a stunning 21-18, 21-18 win over Denmark’s Mia Blichfeldt to set up a clash with China’s Chen Yu Fei.

Ashmita Chaliha won the all-Indian contest against Isharani Baruah 12-21, 21-13, 21-12 and will next take on Japan’s Hina Akechi.

However, Unnati Hooda went down fighting to eighth seed Han Yue of China 21-17, 19-21, 17-21, while Anmol Kharb lost 10-21, 18-21 to fourth seed Tomoka Miyazaki of Japan.

World Championships bronze medallist Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand eased past Hong Kong’s Fan Ka Yan and Leung Yuet Yee 21-16, 21-9 in women’s doubles and will face Americans Lauren Lam and Allison Lee next.

Among other Indians in doubles, Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun lost 20-22, 12-21 to Chinese Taipei’s He Zhi-Wei and Huang Jui-Hsuan.

There was further disappointment in store for Hariharan as he and his mixed doubles partner Tanisha Crasto lost 26-28, 14-21 to Malaysia’s Wong Tien Ci and Lim Chiew Sien.

Dhruv Rawat and K Maneesha also faced defeat, going down 9-21, 15-21 to second seeds Jiang Zhen Bang and Wei Ya Xin of China, while Dhruv Kapila and Radhika Sharma lost 15-21, 10-21 to fourth seeds Guo Xin Wa and Chen Fang Hui of China.

title: Road to World No. 1 Beckons For Andreeva After WTA Finals Triumph
article_text:
Despite her status as a reigning Grand Slam champion, Mirra Andreeva was not named by many as a significant title contender in Indian Wells. Five matches and ten sets later, the 19-year-old had stunned the wider tennis world with one of the most emphatic WTA Finals title runs in history.

Across five matches, Andreeva dropped just 26 games to claim the title on her debut singles appearance at the event. The opening set of her 7-5, 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday’s final was the only time she dropped more than four games in a set, beating the Ukrainian twice in Indian Wells alongside further round-robin victories against Aryna Sabalenka and Diana Shnaider, and a semi-final win versus Jessica Pegula.

Triumph for Andreeva completed a spellbinding year for the Russian, who won four titles in total across the season. Most notably, she captured her first major at the French Open in June and, after starting the year at ninth in the WTA Rankings, she finishes 2026 at a brand new career high of world No. 2.

Her rise to No. 2 in the world is something worthy of celebration in itself, with the Russian moving ahead of the likes of Sabalenka, Coco Gauff, and Iga Swiatek in the WTA pecking order this year. But, having produced arguably the best tennis of her career to sweep aside some of the very best of the women’s game this past week, her pathway to progressing even further and claiming the world No. 1 ranking is now more than set.

The 19-year-old’s unbeaten run at the WTA Finals saw her pick up a staggering 1,500 ranking points, the most points on offer at any tournament outside of the four Grand Slams. Having already banked 2,000 points in June for her Roland Garros victory, and with a tour-leading 55 match wins to her name, Andreeva ends 2026 as the world No. 2 on 7,806 points.

Notably, that leaves her within touching distance of Elena Rybakina, whose status as the year-end No.1 was already secured before she was forced to withdraw from her WTA Finals title defence, struck down by a viral illness. Rybakina’s year was highlighted by her Australian Open and US Open triumphs, as well as lifting WTA 500 titles in Stuttgart and Ningbo. The Kazakh claimed the world No. 1 ranking for the first time alongside her US Open victory in September, usurping Sabalenka.

Rybakina has undoubtedly been the class of the field in 2026, but her WTA Finals withdrawal saw her unable to reclaim any of the 1,500 points she won for her own unbeaten run to the title in Riyadh twelve months ago. Despite winning two majors, she finishes the year only 293 points ahead of Andreeva, with a total of 8,099 points.

Long proclaimed as a future world No.1, Andreeva’s opportunity to sit at the top of the WTA Rankings now beckons sooner rather than later. The Russian is firmly within striking distance of Rybakina and the pair could battle for top spot in the very opening week of the season if, as expected, both compete at the Brisbane International.

Andreeva will then have a full 500 points to defend at the Adelaide International the following week, but has comparatively fewer points to defend at the Australian Open straight afterwards. Beaten in the fourth round by Svitolina this January, she has only 240 ranking points to her name from Melbourne. In contrast, Rybakina has a full 2,000 points on her ranking as the reigning champion, and could lose her world No. 1 ranking to Andreeva even with a successful title defence, should Andreeva go deep into the draw.

It may well not only be the 19-year-old in the hunt for the world No.1 ranking at next year’s Australian Open. World No. 3 Sabalenka, world No. 4 Gauff, and world No. 5 Pegula could well all be in with a mathematical chance come the start of the tournament, though the odds are nowhere near as heavily stacked in their favour as they are for Andreeva. And, if there were any lingering doubts about her mentality and dealing with pressure on the biggest stages, five straight-set wins over top-10 opposition in Indian Wells surely silenced even her strongest of critics.

Ever since her breakout run at the 2023 Madrid Open as a 16-year-old, people have wondered if Andreeva could one day be the world No. 1. Now, it appears to be more of a question of when, and how soon, she will start her reign at the very top of women's tennis.

Oli Dickson Jefford is a freelance sports journalist, specialising in tennis. Having achieved a gold standard NCTJ qualification in the UK, he has previously worked full-time for Beat Media Group and Tennis365. He has attended Wimbledon three times as an accredited journalist as well as the Queen's Club Championships.

title: Hong Kong Open 2026 badminton: Kidambi Srikanth, Rakshitha Ramraj stun higher-ranked opponents

title: Smashing Stats: Hong Kong Open 2026
article_text:
Xie Xingfang, the last women's singles player to win consecutive editions, celebrates her second title in 2007.

With the final HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 spots on the line, LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 plays a decisive role in this season’s conclusion.

Here are the key numbers and storylines to watch as the tournament marks its final year as a Super 500 event.

Top seeds Wang Zhi Yi, Yuki Fukushima and Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping have all tasted past success in Hong Kong.

Wang and Feng/Huang are two of the three defending champions returning, alongside fellow Chinese stars Liang Wei Keng/Wang Chang.

Glory for second seed Wang will make her the first women’s singles player since Tai Tzu Ying in 2017 to win consecutive editions.

She could also emulate Xie Xingfang, the last Chinese to win the category twice in a row in 2007.

Fukushima, now partnering Mayu Matsumoto, won in 2018 with Sayaka Hirota.

Japan boast three seeded pairs in women’s doubles this time as they look to end a drought in the category stretching back to Fukushima and Hirota’s triumph.

Men’s singles second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn aims to expand Thailand’s winners list by replicating their solitary victory in 2001 via Sujitra Ekmongkolpaisarn in women’s singles.

Indonesia are yet to produce a champion in women’s singles, in which they possess sixth seed Putri Kusuma Wardani.

Wardani has an added incentive this year – winning the title could mean qualification to the World Tour Finals.

Likewise, Koki Watanabe could achieve both – for self and country – if he triumphs in men’s singles.

Men’s singles has featured remarkable parity, with players representing six different flags topping the podium across the last six editions.

Malaysia, who havenot had success in men’s doubles since 1999 (Cheah Soon Kit/Yap Kim Hock), count on eighth seeds Man Wei Chong/Tee Kai Wun and Aaron Tai/Yap Roy King.

China are the sole nation to celebrate podium toppers at the last four Hong Kong Opens.

Standout Stat: Since 2011, Chinese mixed pairs have won eight of the 12 editions – a 66.7 per cent strike rate that stands as the joint-highest across all five categories during that span.

title: 2026 Nitto ATP Finals Prize Pool Breakdown
article_text:
The Nitto ATP Finals will take place from November 15 - 22, 2026, at the Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy.

This year's edition features a record total prize pool of $15,750,000, up from $15,500,000 last year.

The 2026 undefeated singles champion will earn $5,171,000, while the undefeated doubles team will share $959,300. In 2025, Jannik Sinner became the undefeated singles champion for the second consecutive year, setting the record for the highest single-tournament payout of all time at $5,071,000.

title: Doubles players at ATP Finals take issue with tour leaders as contentious reforms are voted on
Rising star Fils earns first ATP Finals win
article_text:
Rising star Arthur Fils claimed his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin.

Fils, 22, beat 20-year-old Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2 to become the first Frenchman to record an ATP Finals victory since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011.

It was the youngest match by combined age at the season-ending tournament - which features the eight top-performing men - since a 21-year-old Novak Djokovic defeated a 20-year-old Juan Martin del Potro in 2008.

Fils has risen to a career-high ranking of seventh in the world during a season in which he became the youngest French ATP Masters 1000 champion in Cincinnati.

All four debutants at this year's tournament lost their opening match, with Fils beaten by American third seed Ben Shelton and Spain's Jodar losing to Alexander Zverev in the John McEnroe Group.

But Fils, a finalist at the Next Gen ATP Finals three years ago, will fight for a place in the semi-finals against world number one Zverev on Thursday after keeping alive his hopes of reaching the knockout stage on his debut.

"It's going to be tough but I know that I can battle. I'm not afraid," said Fils of his showdown with Zverev, who plays Shelton later on Tuesday.

"It will be a nice match against the world number one. I don't have anything to lose, I'm just going to enjoy myself."

Fils was second best in the first set but gradually found his rhythm to outperform a fading Jodar over sets two and three.

Jodar made an ideal start, striking at the perfect moment when he broke for the first time to clinch the opening set after 10 games.

Fils particularly struggled on serve, landing just 38% of first serves in, and produced just a single winner in a flat first set.

But the Frenchman reset impressively in the second, twice breaking Jodar's serve on his way to forcing a decider.

Jodar appeared to be fading physically and took a medical timeout after falling a double break behind in the second set.

The Spaniard was unable to rediscover his previous level, however, and Fils powered to victory by winning six of the final seven games.

"It means a lot to me after a tough start," Fils said.

"I played a great game against Ben [Shelton], I was just unlucky. The first set here was frustrating and I was struggling - but I'm very happy with the second and third."

In the men's doubles, Britain's Henry Patten and Finnish team-mate Harri Heliovaara fell to defeat in their second match.

The world number ones and defending champions won the first set but were beaten 6-7 (5-7) 6-3 10-4 by fourth seeds Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic.

- Indian mixed doubles shuttlers Dhruv Kapila and Radhika Sharma advanced to the semifinals of the Hong Kong Super 500 qualifiers on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, registering a dominant straight-game win over local rivals Ying Kit Cheng and Yuet Yee Leung.

- Playing on Court 1, the Indian duo wrapped up the contest 21-17, 21-17 in just 36 minutes to book their berth in the main draw of the BWF World Tour Super 500 tournament, where they are slated to meet fourth seeds Guo Xinwa and Chen Fanghui of China in the opening round.

- The positive start in the qualifiers accompanied a strong opening day for the Indian contingent, with fifth-seeded men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty edging past Chinese Taipei's Lee Jhe-Huei and Yang Po-Hsuan in three games, while in-form men's singles shuttler Lakshya Sen prepares to chase his third consecutive tour title.

title: Alexander Zverev told tennis would be ‘better off without him’ amid ATP Finals bid and new lawsuit
article_text:
A vocal critic of Alexander Zverev believes tennis would be “better off without him” amid the world No 1 facing a new lawsuit from an ex-partner.

In June 2024, criminal proceedings against Zverev over allegations that he pushed and strangled his then-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, were discontinued by a Berlin court following a settlement.

The 6ft 6in player denied the allegations, and court proceedings ended without a verdict or finding of guilt. Under the agreement, though, Zverev was ordered to pay €150,000 to the state and a further €50,000 to charitable organisations.

This summer, Zverev stated the accusations against him “have been proven false” and that his “innocence has been proven”. Last week, though, reports emerged that Patea, who is the mother of his five-year-old daughter, was suing the two-time major winner off the back of those comments.

According to Bounces, Patea has filed a new civil lawsuit against the 29-year-old over alleged ‘false statements’ made in that interview with L’Equipe in June. The report states the Berlin court assigned the case a number and issued a procedural order on 5 November. However, the lawsuit has not yet been formally served on Zverev.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

According to Patea’s lawyer, Michael Scheele, Zverev’s remarks constitute a ‘serious infringement’ of their settlement agreement, and she is seeking compensation for the alleged damage to her public standing.

Now, Caitlyn Thompson, who is a co-host on The Rennae Stubbs Tennis Podcast, went as far as saying that tennis would be better off without Zverev, who is the year-end No 1 and won the French Open and US Open in 2026.

The co-founder of Racquet magazine has been an outspoken critic of Zverev, who also previously faced allegations of domestic abuse by his former girlfriend and tennis player, Olga Sharypova. On that, the ATP halted its investigation into those claims in January 2023 after more than two years due to insufficient evidence.

Thompson said on the podcast, “I think if you settle a case out of court by making payments to domestic violence shelters and part of that is you neither admit guilt nor are granted innocence, but you go on a tour where you tell everyone that you are innocent.

“Legally, seems like there are consequences. So she is suing him because he has been claiming that he was found innocent, which is not true; he was found neither. And it was a lot to settle. The Tour would be better off without him, and that’s it.”

Serena Williams’ coach, Stubbs, agreed with the latter bit, before Thompson admitted she is hopeful that Carlos Alcaraz, who she sees as the true best player in the world, beats Zverev at the ATP Finals this week.

She added, “And now hopefully the No 1 player in the world in facts will beat the No 1 player in numbers, and we can just see how deserving he is of the world No 1 status at the end of this tournament, which I think we all know is not deserving.”

Many have argued that Zverev’s No 1 status has an asterisk next to it as he won his two Grand Slams without having to go through either Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner, both of whom missed many months this season due to injury.

Conversely, others argue that staying fit is part of tennis and you can only beat what is in front of you.

title: Hong Kong Open: Men’s Doubles Completes Hangzhou Cast
article_text:
Men’s doubles became the first discipline to lock in all eight qualifiers for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 following a dramatic opening day at LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Tuesday.

Four pairs – Ben Lane/Sean Vendy, Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri, Daniel Lundgaard/Mads Vestergaard, and Chen Bo Yang/Liu Yi – punched their tickets to the season finale following the first round exits of direct challengers Sabar Karyaman Gutama/Moh Reza Pahlevi Isfahani and Raymond Indra/Nikolaus Joaquin.

For Vendy, returning to the prestigious year-end event after five years carries far greater weight than his and Lane’s previous appearance.

“The last time (in January 2021) wasn’t a true representation of the season because it was during COVID – many of the Chinese players weren’t competing and the tournaments were generally weaker,” Vendy reflected. “Honestly, we weren’t at the level required to qualify back then.

“This has been a long time coming. Only the top eight pairs make the Finals, so it’s no easy feat. Qualifying this time around, against a full-strength field over a full year, is something we are really proud of.”

While Lundgaard/Vestergaard and Chen/Liu clinched their maiden appearances at a season finale, Tuesday proved bittersweet for the Indonesian camp. Shortly after Alfian and Fikri’s spot became certain, compatriots Gutama and Isfahani saw their own qualifying hopes dashed by fellow Indonesians Daniel Marthin/Leo Rolly Carnando, who won 21-13 21-15.

In women’s doubles, the Race to Finals remains open, though Lauren Lam and Allison Lee took a massive step toward making history as the first American pair to qualify for a season finale. In a high-stakes showdown against direct rivals Febriana Dwipuji Kusuma/Meilysa Trias Puspitasari, Lam and Lee held their nerve to secure a hard-fought 21-16 13-21 21-15 win.

“A lot of eyes were on this match because of the race, so there were plenty of nerves going into it,” Lee admitted. “I don’t think it was just us, those two obviously had a lot of pressure too, so I had to keep that in mind as well.”

Combined with the loss of Chinese Taipei’s Hsu Ya Ching/Sung Yu Hsuan, the battle for the final three women’s doubles spots has narrowed to a four-way race between Lam/Lee, Hsu Yin Hui/Lin Jhih Yun, Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva and Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti.

Despite standing on the brink of a landmark achievement for US badminton, Lee is keeping her focus firmly on the court.

“It doesn’t feel real so sometimes I don’t even think about it until it actually happens,” Lee said. “There’s only one way to wait for it and that’s to keep going until the end.”

title: Mirra Andreeva accused of ‘deliberate manipulation’ at WTA Finals by Elina Svitolina’s coach
article_text:
Mirra Andreeva has faced a strong accusation from a former Ukrainian tennis star following her victory over Elina Svitolina at the 2026 WTA Finals.

Andreeva defeated Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in the final at the WTA’s season-ending championships in Indian Wells last week.

The 19-year-old Russian, who was making her WTA Finals debut, did not drop a set across her five matches during a dominant run to the title.

Since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Svitolina has opted not to shake hands with players from Russia or Belarus (a Russian ally) before or after matches.

The 32-year-old Ukrainian chose not to mention Andreeva in her speech during the trophy ceremony after the WTA Finals final.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Andreeva, though, had some warm words for Svitolina during her speech.

“I just want to congratulate Elina and the team for an amazing week,” said the French Open champion and world No 2.

“You had an amazing season, I know it’s tough to lose in the final but you had such an amazing season.

“You have a young daughter, you are an amazing Mom to come back and do this. It’s super hard.

“I would not know how hard it is to come back and do that, so congratulations for that and to your team as well. I wish you the best of luck for next season.”

Russian president Vladimir Putin released a statement to congratulate Andreeva on her WTA Finals title.

“With your brilliant and convincing victory, you have carried on the remarkable traditions of Russian tennis,” Putin was quoted as saying by the Russian Embassy in South Africa. “I wish you continued success and all the very best.”

Sergiy Stakhovsky, a former Ukrainian ATP Tour player who retired in 2022, coached Svitolina ahead of and during the WTA Finals.

Svitolina’s long-time coach Andrew Bettles was not with her in Indian Wells as his wife was expecting a baby.

In a post on X/Twitter, Stakhovsky slammed those who have described Andreeva congratulating Svitolina as an “act of class.”

Stakhovsky wrote: “Congratulating Elina, but overlooking the fact that her country invaded Ukraine, murdered hundreds of thousands of people, never publicly condemning the war, and on top receiving honours from the hands of putin, is not an act of “CLASS”…. It an act of DELIBERATE MANIPULATION.”

title: Satwik-Chirag Survive Major Scare To Win Thrilling Hong Kong Open Opener, Dhruv-Radhika Advance
article_text:
Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty survive a major scare, saving four match points to beat Chinese Taipei's Lee-Yang pair in a thrilling Hong Kong Open opener.

India’s star men’s doubles duo of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty overcame a stiff challenge from Chinese Taipei’s Jhe-Huei Lee and Po-Hsuan Yang to clinch a hard-fought three-game win in their Hong Kong Super 500 opener on Tuesday.

Satwik-Chirag dropped the opening game but bounced back to take the second before displaying tremendous composure to save four match points and seal a thrilling 15-21, 21-17, 28-26 win in a 68-minute battle.

Earlier, India’s mixed doubles duo of Dhruv Kapila and Radhika Sharma booked their place in the main draw with a straight-games 21-17, 21-17 win against Hong Kong’s Ying Kit Cheng and Yuet Yee Leung in the qualifiers.

The Indian duo will face fourth-seeded China’s Guo Xin Wa and Chen Fang Hui.

Satwik and Chirag, who have claimed two titles this season, enjoyed a dominant 7-0 head-to-head record against Lee and Yang heading into the clash.

It turned out to be an absorbing contest, with the momentum swinging repeatedly between the two pairs.

The Indians squandered a 9-6 lead in the opening game as the Chinese Taipei duo pulled away from 15-all to take the lead.

Lee and Yang carried their momentum into the second game, opening up a 6-3 lead. But Satwik and Chirag fought back with three consecutive points to draw level before the two pairs traded points in a closely contested battle that remained tied at 11-all.

Satwik and Chirag then shifted gears to open up a 16-11 lead, only for the Chinese Taipei pair to fight back and cut the deficit to 16-18. The Indians, though, kept their composure to clinch the game and take the match into a decider.

The third game tested the mental fortitude of both pairs, with neither able to establish a decisive advantage.

Lee and Yang raced to a 6-3 lead, but the contest remained neck-and-neck thereafter. Satwik and Chirag earned two match points but couldn’t convert either, before missing out on further chances to close out the match.

Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty overcame a stiff challenge from Chinese Taipei's Jhe-Huei Lee and Po-Hsuan Yang, bouncing back from a first-game loss to save four match points and secure a thrilling 15-21, 21-17, 28-26 victory.

title: Golf: Golf-DeChambeau to join DP World Tour after LIV collapse
article_text:
LONDON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - American Bryson DeChambeau will bring his big-hitting game to the DP World Tour next season after the collapse of LIV Golf, the European organisation said on Tuesday.

The 33-year-old DeChambeau, a two-time US Open champion, was one of the highest-profile players to leave the PGA Tour for the Saudi-backed venture four years ago.

DeChambeau's move is the latest boost for the DP World Tour which also announced that major champions Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Bubba Watson have signed agreements to receive invitations to a specific number of tournaments next season.

Spain's twice major winner Jon Rahm, who also defected to LIV Golf, sealed a triumphant return to the DP World Tour this month by winning the Abu Dhabi Championship. Briton Tyrrell Hatton and Spaniard Sergio Garcia are also rejoining the European Tour.

"The addition of Bryson DeChambeau joining as a member for the first time in Category 1 takes the total of major champions in exempt membership to 22 for the 2027 season," the DP World Tour said in a statement.

LIV Golf, which shook professional golf to its foundations when it launched its breakaway tour in 2022, announced this month that it would begin winding down operations after losing key players and the funding needed to continue operating.

DeChambeau was a staunch LIV Golf loyalist but its demise meant his future was unclear.

He was ineligible to return to the US PGA Tour for at least 12 months after his last appearance for LIV Golf.

DeChambeau has been welcomed by the DP World Tour, though, and his 2024 US Open victory ensures him Category 1 status, meaning he can play as many events as he chooses.

World number two Rory McIlroy has been a fierce critic of LIV Golf and has had a frosty relationship with DeChambeau but said this month the American would add interest to the DP World Tour.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," McIlroy said.

DeChambeau finished 14th at the British Open at Royal Birkdale this year after being docked two shots in his second round after video footage showed he improved his swing path by trampling down grass at the fifth hole.

While he can be a divisive personality, DeChambeau is generally popular with galleries and has his own YouTube channel with more than 3 million subscribers.

title: Hong Kong Open 2026 badminton: Satwik-Chirag end losing streak with thrilling first-round win
Emma Raducanu Set for 2027 Comeback as She Eyes a Fresh Start
article_text:
Emma Raducanu is set to return to tennis at the 2027 United Cup in Australia, ending a six-month absence from the sport.

The British star is expected to begin her new season at the mixed-team competition in early January, as she looks to put her injury struggles behind her and regain momentum ahead of the Australian Open.

The 2021 US Open champion has been out of competition since June with a shin stress fracture. In her last match, she faced 2024 Olympic silver medalist Donna Vekic in the Queen’s Club Championships final, where she lost in straight sets to the Croatian in her first grass-court final.

Just 14 days after the match, Raducanu withdrew from Wimbledon ahead of her opening-round match. The injury subsequently ruled her out for the rest of the season, forcing the 23-year-old to prioritize recovery rather than risk an early return to competition.

Raducanu will be able to use a special ranking of 38 to enter tournaments. This provision is available to players sidelined for at least six months due to injury and allows them to use their pre-absence ranking when entering selected events.

The special ranking will be particularly valuable for the British player, allowing her to enter eight events next year, including two Grand Slams and five WTA 1000 events. This could provide crucial support as Raducanu rebuilds her position and returns to competing regularly against the world’s best players.

The British number five will make her comeback at the United Cup, where she is set to face France’s Diane Parry. Raducanu will be joined by Arthur Fery, Francesca Jones, Jan Choinski, Neal Skupski and Olivia Nicholls in the Great Britain squad.

The British team has been drawn in Group D alongside Australia and France, with the group-stage matches taking place in Sydney. The competition will give Raducanu a chance to regain confidence and test herself against international opposition ahead of the first Grand Slam of the season.

Since winning the 2021 US Open, the Brit has struggled to maintain consistency, with several physical setbacks and recovery periods interrupting her progress on the WTA Tour.

Raducanu will head into the upcoming season with an opportunity to put a difficult period behind her. The former World No. 10 has already shown she can challenge the best players on tour, but finding sustained form will be key to taking the next step in 2027.

title: “Another Glorious Moment for Indian Badminton”: Mansukh Mandaviya Hails Lakshya Sen After Historic Japan Masters Win
GB's Patten criticises ATP chairman and CEO for absence
article_text:
Britain's top-ranked doubles player Henry Patten criticised the ATP's chairman and CEO for their absence at Monday's year-end world number one trophy presentation.

Wimbledon champions Patten and Finnish team-mate Harri Heliovaara received their trophy from the ATP's chief tour officer Andre Silva in Turin, after ending the season as the top-ranked men's doubles pairing for the first time.

In his acceptance speech, Patten, 30, called out ATP chairman Andrea Gaudenzi and CEO Eno Polo for their decision not to attend.

"What a journey it has been. Turin is such a special place for us, we played a challenger just across the road when we ranked 60 and 40 in the world a couple of years ago. I never would have dreamt that we would be in the position that we're in now," said Patten.

"For us it's a really big deal. It's a real shame that the ATP chairman and the ATP CEO don't think the same.

"It would have been nice to have them on court with us today, but here we are by ourselves.

"We have worked incredibly hard and thank you all for appreciating that."

BBC Sport has contacted the ATP Tour for comment.

It is crystal clear why Patten decided he needed to dig out ATP bosses Gaudenzi and Polo.

Patten, Heliovaara and the rest of the men's doubles cohort believe their governing body simply does not care about their discipline.

And, as Patten barely concealed in his pointed speech, the non-appearance of Gaudenzi and Polo underlined what the players believe is a lack of respect.

In July, the ATP made proposals to halve doubles draws at its flagship Masters 1000 events to 16 teams. Smaller tournaments would be reduced to eight teams.

That would see the percentage of prize money devoted to doubles events falling from 20% to 10%, with the difference redistributed to singles players.

The plans drew the fury of doubles players, who believe the "drastic" changes could kill the format. Patten also used his Wimbledon victory speech to passionately point out the importance of doubles.

The ATP says it wants to create "a more sustainable long-term model" for the men's tour, insisting it wants to "maintain the important role" of doubles.

The tour's board - comprised of chairman Gaudenzi, four tournament representatives and four player representatives - will vote on the plans in Turin this week.

Gaudenzi and Polo are spending much of their week in those meetings.

The decision will shape the future of men's doubles, along with the careers and lives of its players.

By speaking out again now, Patten's barbed comments were interpreted to be timely, in an attempt to apply more pressure before the ATP board meets on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Tiger Woods announces new project ahead of PGA Tour return
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

- Tiger Woods has announced plans to design a £30 million championship-level links golf course at Bellarena on Northern Ireland's Causeway Coast, marking the region's first such development in over a century.

- The project is being spearheaded by hospitality group Galgorm Collection, with construction expected to commence next year provided all necessary planning approvals are granted.

- Situated approximately 20 miles from Royal Portrush, the proposed course is intended to challenge the world's best golfers while appearing as a natural part of the coastline.

- The 15-time major champion is also set to make his competitive return to golf after an absence of over two years at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas this December.

- Woods' hiatus from competitive play followed three surgeries and a stint in a rehabilitation facility after being charged with driving under the influence in Florida.

title: Tiger Woods: Former world No 1 hails 'special opportunity' to design new course in Northern Ireland with TGR Design
article_text:
Tiger Woods has revealed he will design the first championship-standard links golf course built in Northern Ireland for more than 100 years, describing the project as a "special opportunity".

Reports linking the 15-time major champion with the proposed £30 million course at Bellarena on the north west coast between Limavady and Coleraine had been circulating for several weeks, ahead of Thursday's official announcement.

Hospitality group Galgorm Collection is building the course, with construction set to get under way next year if the required planning approvals are secured.

In a statement, Woods said: "Northern Ireland is home to some of the greatest links golf in the world, and building one on the Causeway Coast is a special opportunity for our team.

"We want Bellarena to feel as though it has always been part of this coastline, with a course that challenges the best players and is fun for everyone who plays it."

Colin Johnston, chief executive of Galgorm Collection, announced that Woods and his TGR Design firm would craft the new links layout.

"Set against the spectacular backdrop of Northern Ireland's rugged northwest coast, our plans represent a once-in-a-generation opportunity to transform Northern Ireland's golfing and tourism future," Johnston said.

Bellarena is around 20 miles from Royal Portrush Golf Club, which hosted Shane Lowry's win at The Open in 2019 and Scottie Scheffler completing the third leg of the career Grand Slam in 2025.

Portstewart - host of Jon Rahm's win at the 2017 Irish Open - and Castlerock also boast acclaimed links courses in the region.

Reef Destinations has previously worked with TGR Design on course construction projects in the United States. Bellarena already has a historical link with the United States as a site of a US Army base during the Second World War.

Woods is poised to return to competitive golf next month for the first time in over two years after being confirmed as an entrant at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas from December 3-6.

The 50-year-old has not played competitively since The Open at Royal Troon in 2024 and has played limited golf since a career-threatening car crash in Florida in 2021.

Woods has had at least three different surgeries since his last start and spent time at a rehab facility in Switzerland earlier this year, having been arrested and charged with driving under the influence following a car crash near his home.
