title: DP World Tour Play-Offs: Race to Dubai battle and PGA Tour dual member cards decided in compelling climax
article_text:
In a gripping climax to the DP World Tour season, the destiny of the 2026 Race to Dubai title went down to the final hole.

For a time during Sunday's final round at the DP World Tour Championship, just one-tenth of a point separated Eugenio Chacarra and Rory McIlroy as the pair battled for the Race to Dubai crown.

With Tyrrell Hatton playing his way to a commanding victory, all eyes were on who would claim the Harry Vardon Trophy as the Tour's best-performing player across the 42-event campaign.

At the end of a day that saw the overall lead in the Rankings chop and change with remarkable regularity, McIlroy celebrated drawing level with Colin Montgomerie on eight Race to Dubai titles as Chacarra fell just short despite a breakthrough campaign.

Ahead of the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, the penultimate event of the season, earlier this month, Chacarra entered the closing stretch as the man in pole position.

With three wins to his name, the Spaniard led from Patrick Reed and McIlroy in third as the main protagonists in the contest to be crowned European Number One.

Holding a lead of 669 points over Reed in second, and a cushion of just under 1,000 points above McIlroy in third, there were even scenarios where Chacarra could wrap up matters with a win at Yas Links.

But come the close of proceedings in Abu Dhabi, McIlroy had closed the gap by almost half to 533.93 points with a third-place finish.

Reed, by contrast, finished in a tie for 43rd and arrived for the second of back-to-back Rolex Series events requiring at worst to finish in a two-way tie for second to stand a chance of winning the Race to Dubai.

But after scores of 75 and 77 over the opening two rounds over the Earth course at Jumeirah Golf Estates, the American was out of the picture and it was all down to Chacarra and McIlroy over the weekend.

After the third round, things looked favourable for Chacarra as he and McIlroy - a repeat winner at the Masters Tournament in April - both sat in a tie for fourth at five under.

To add to the drama, McIlroy and Chacarra were separated by just one group on the final day, with the latter having to react at every step.

But Chacarra appeared unfazed, making four birdies across his opening eight holes, before a run of three bogeys around the turn halted his momentum. To his credit, he birdied the 13th and 14th and was back into the lead on the Rankings.

The telling moment came at the 16th, when McIlroy set up a birdie - his lone gain on the back nine - to move back ahead as the gutsy Chacarra could only par his closing three holes.

With that, and with Mikael Lindberg and then Victor Perez unable to match or better McIlroy's total of ten under for the week, the celebrations began.

"This is probably a good thing, but I wasn't aware of how much it was sort of going back and forth until the 16th," McIlroy later reflected of his closing bogey-free 67.

"When I was walking to the green, I saw that he was projected first. Then when I made my birdie and I'm walking off the green, I saw I was projected first. I was a little nervous going to the last couple of holes.

"I guess I did what I needed to do and I shot a good score today. A lot of other things went my way today, as well.

"No one made a run. Eugenio played pretty good but none of the chasing pack did anything... thankfully everything fell my way today."

Another intriguing subplot across the Play-Offs surrounded which players would have dual membership with the PGA Tour next season.

While for Chacarra and Reed it was all but a formality, along with other multiple winners across the campaign in South African pair Casey Jarvis and Jayden Schaper, others still had more substantial work to do.

Another player who appeared comfortable was Jacob Skov Olesen - a graduate of Qualifying School in 2024 - as he produced a run of consistent form, including a runner-up finish among two top tens across the Back 9.

Daniel Hillier was also feeling fairly comfortable aheading into the Play-Offs. On the bubble for much of the Back 9, a runner-up finish - a third of his campaign - at the DP World India Championship backed up by a top-15 finish at the Genesis Championship helped the New Zealander arrive in the UAE shorn of the stress he faced last year when he missed out by one spot.

The player to face the biggest case of heartbreak this time was Mikael Lindberg.

A breakthrough DP World Tour winner in Türkiye earlier in the season, the Swede was projected to finish among the top ten non exempt performers on the Race to Dubai Rankings for much of the final round in Dubai before a bogey-bogey finish dropped him outside the group of qualifying players.

His missed opportunity benefited Joe Dean, with the Englishman able to breathe a sigh of relief after a closing 74 had left his status in doubt.

For Bernd Wiesberger, a top-five finish in Abu Dhabi helped his cause no end, while fellow former Ryder Cupper Andy Sullivan closed out his season with back-to-back top-15 finishes to land him full status on the PGA Tour for the first time.

title: 'Clearer' approach has lifted England mood
article_text:
Captain Maro Itoje says a clearer sense of purpose and unity has coincided with improved performances from England this autumn.

They have won their last four games, racking up victories over Fiji, Argentina, Australia and Japan in the Nations Championship.

Prior to that run, England had lost five successive Tests - a streak that included their worst ever Six Nations campaign.

They host New Zealand on Saturday, with the All Blacks stung by their first defeat by Wales in 73 years last time out.

"It feels a lot more cohesive," Itoje told BBC Rugby Union Weekly.

"It feels, from a player's point of view, that our understanding of what we're trying to do is a lot clearer.

"The level of understanding has grown from campaign to campaign and we have a very clear sense of what we're doing, what we're trying to do and we're getting into those positions a lot more effectively now."

A Times report earlier this month, external claimed senior players had sought a summit meeting with head coach Steve Borthwick after their July Nations Championship campaign due to differences of opinion over the team's direction.

Itoje was rested for that tour and Jamie George, who had reassumed the captaincy in his absence, said parts of the article were untrue and the squad were "incredibly disappointed" by its publication.

"As senior players part of our job is to challenge Steve," said George at the time. "Steve is so open to us giving feedback and having challenge."

In turn, Borthwick has credited his senior players with leading a drive on discipline that has helped England's results turn a corner.

Across their first eight Tests in 2026, England were shown 14 yellow cards and a red.

It was highlighted as a key area to improve before the autumn and they have responded with no cards and only 15 penalties conceded across their two November Tests so far.

"It's never just one thing, but I will talk about one matter," added Borthwick of the reasons behind the improvement.

"A number of weeks ago, the senior players led the players in groups. It was a big discussion topic and coming out it was a series of commitments that the players made about what they need to do.

"They've backed up those commitments in this first couple weeks. Now we know that's going be tested even more this weekend."

Itoje admitted the arrival of New Zealand brought a different atmosphere to training.

"There are weeks...and then there are weeks," he said.

"The step-up often first starts with the mind, then goes down to behaviours and actions.

"There's a sharpness needed when playing against a team like New Zealand that for other games you may not need to get to.

"Without any disrespect, when you play in New Zealand your mind has to be sharper than when you play a team like Japan."

Before the final round of matches and Nations Championship finals weekend, New Zealand lead the southern hemisphere standings, putting them on course for the title decider at Allianz Stadium on 29 November.

South Africa, who are a point behind in the table and could overtake the All Blacks if they slip up at Twickenham on Saturday, visit Ireland later in the day.

The build-up in Dublin has been dominated by Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus' criticism of match officials and subsequent six-Test ban.

While Borthwick would not be drawn on Erasmus' situation or comments, he stressed the importance of respect for referees and their colleagues.

"When I first picked up a rugby ball aged 11, my schoolteacher told me, 'you call the referee sir'," he added.

"For so many years I still called the referees sir, because it's just so well ingrained. For this brilliant sport we're involved in, respect is integral. It is different to other sports and it's one of the reasons I love it."

title: Gloucester-Hartpury boss Murphy exits on eve of new season
article_text:
Gloucester-Hartpury head of rugby Dan Murphy has left the club on the eve of the new Premiership Women's Rugby season.

Murphy took over last season, following the departure of Sean Lynn for the Wales head coach role, and had previously spent four years with the club as scrum coach.

Three-time champions Gloucester-Hartpury finished top of the regular-season table last term but failed to reach the PWR final for the first time in four years after being beaten by Saracens in the semi-finals.

They open their 2026-27 campaign on Saturday away to Sale Sharks.

"We recognise that the timing of this change, immediately before the start of the season, is not ideal," a club statement said., external

"However, this decision ensures stability for the squad ahead of an important first game."

The statement added the decision was made following a "review of the programme".

"The club believes the change is in Gloucester-Hartpury's best interests," it continued.

Murphy's departure follows the exit of backs and attack coach Matt Banahan at the end of last season.

The remaining coaching team will take charge for the upcoming match, with former London Irish captain Luke Narraway joining as consultant coach while the long-term structure of the team is decided.

Gloucester-Hartpury won 14 consecutive league games in 2025-26 to storm once again to the top of the table.

However, defeats in their final two games of the campaign, before a semi-final loss to Trailfinders, meant their season ended on a muted note after a run of three championship triumphs.

They have also lost a number of influential players over the summer, including mainstays of the club as it grew into the league's dominant force in recent seasons.

England captain Zoe Stratford and fellow Red Roses centre Tatyana Heard, back-row forward Sarah Beckett and Wales hooker Kelsey Jones have all joined Saturday's opponents Sale, while Wales back-row Bethan Lewis left for Bristol.

Murphy added in a statement: "I would like to place on record my thanks to the players, staff and loyal fans for their support throughout my time at Gloucester-Hartpury.

"I wish everyone at the club all the best for the future."

title: Unbeaten World Rugby Nations Cup winners name teams for final bout
article_text:
The winners of Pools A and B in the World Rugby Nations Cup will meet in Tbilisi this weekend for bragging rights as the tournament’s best.

The USA enjoyed a blowout win over Romania in round 5 to secure their Pool A crown after four tight wins to begin the inaugural competition, while Georgia’s supremacy in Pool B has never been challenged, and they’ve emerged with a competition-best points differential of +124 through five rounds of action.

There is no further silverware on offer for the teams, but there’s an air of serendipity in the matchup coming in the final round of the competition.

USA head coach Scott Lawrence has made just one change to the starting XV that put 53 points on Romania last weekend, with Mitch Wilson replacing Perry Mayo at fullback. And Georgia’s Pierre-Henry Broncan has also opted for as much continuity as possible, only promoting loosehead prop Sergo Abramishvili and halfback Gela Aprasidzeto to the starting team.

title: A 15-year ATP Tour streak has just been broken by Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, and Alexander Zverev
article_text:
Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, and Jannik Sinner have comfortably been the best three players on the ATP Tour this year.

Zverev has managed to claim the first two Grand Slam titles of his career, which subsequently helped him become world No 1 for the first time too.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, began the year with an Australian Open victory, before ending the year on a high with wins in Vienna and Paris after a four and a half month injury absence.

Sinner, too, has suffered with injuries, but he was still able to win the first five Masters titles of the season, as well as his fifth Grand Slam at Wimbledon.

The pair are far and away the top three ranked players on the ATP Tour, as they have been for the past three seasons.

Zverev, Alcaraz, and Sinner have become the first trio of players in 11 years to keep their place in the top three of the rankings for three consecutive seasons.

The last trio to do so was, unsurprisingly, Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer, and Rafael Nadal, who stayed top three for five years in a row between 2007 and 2011.

Zverev, Alcaraz, and Sinner have become just the third trio in men’s tennis history to earn the accolade, also joining Jimmy Connors, Ivan Lendl, and John McEnroe.

Those three tennis legends stayed in the top three between the 1981 and 1984 season, so the current best three players in the world are in very good company.

There is little reason to believe that they will not continue that form into the 2027 season either, particularly with how this season has gone.

Sinner has missed six months of action and Alcaraz has missed four and a half months and yet neither came anywhere near close to losing their position in the top three of the ATP Tour rankings.

As things stand, Alcaraz, who is the current world No 3, sits 1200 ranking points above Ben Shelton in the rankings, and that looks destined to increase at the ATP Finals.

A potential hamstring injury aside, Alcaraz is one of the major favourites to win the ATP Finals and it would be a big surprise to not see him make the final.

The Spaniard could create yet more distance between world No 3 and world No 4 as the 2026 season draws to a close.

It’s hard to see anyone having the consistency to dislodge Zverev, Sinner, and Alcaraz from the rankings, despite the likes of Shelton, Arthur Fils, and Flavio Cobolli making giant strides in the rankings this season.

title: England's Hull one stroke off lead at lucrative LPGA finale
article_text:
England's Charley Hull carded a six-under-par 66 to sit one shot off the first-round lead at the LPGA's lucrative season-ending CME Group Tour Championship.

Australia's Karis Davidson, South Korea's Kim A-lim and Thailand's Jeeno Thitikul, set the pace at seven under at the Tiburon Golf Club in Naples, Florida.

World number two Thitikul, who is aiming to win the event for the third consecutive season, responded to a bogey on the 12th hole by knocking in five consecutive birdies on the back nine.

Hull, who triumphed a decade ago, is one of nine players a stroke behind the leading trio on a stacked leaderboard that contains the top 60 in this season's points list, who are all chasing the $4m (£3.05m) top prize.

"When I won 10 years ago I didn't really take golf seriously. I remember coming into this event when I won, hungover," Hull said.

"I felt pretty good [today]. I kind of like lost my swing feels [at the] end of last week because my hip was very tight, and it just like started rerouting my golf swing," Hull said.

"Today I was nervous on the first tee. I felt like I had no swing feeling. Then as the round developed I felt like I hit it really nice."

Hull's compatriot Lottie Woad made six birdies and a bogey as she signed for five-under 67, along with France's Celine Boutier.

World number one Nelly Korda, who will qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame if she wins on Sunday, endured a mixed day but picked up shots on the 17th and 18th as she finished on four under.

With an $11m purse on offer, Korda would also break Annika Sorenstam's career earnings record if she finishes in sixth place or better.

The Swede amassed 10 major titles and earned $22,583,694 during a storied career before retiring in 2008, with Korda now just under $160,000 behind that mark.

title: USA Names 1st Roster of HSBC SVNS Season
article_text:
The USA Women’s Eagles have named their roster for the opening leg of the 2026-2027 HSBC SVSN season in Dubai. The tournament kicks off Saturday, Nov. 28, and the Americans will do work in Pool A against Spain, Australia and France. All action will be broadcast live on Paramount+. [lead photo: Alex Ho @hoiho_photo]

“We’ve framed the whole cycle as building our house,” head coach Emilie Bydwell looked at the four years between Olympics. “2025 was about forming and foundation building, identifying our new group, and building depth while Paris Olympians took extended breaks or recovered. Last year was about framing our house; getting stability in our squad profile and game model for LA.

“This year is about storm-proofing that performance and building the squad,” the coach continued. “If we have injuries to experienced players, or teams start to figure out how we’re playing, we want to be able to adapt by deploying different roles and combinations. Our goal is to be a really adaptable and anti-fragile team through these first four tournaments and build squad capabilities regardless of the mix of experienced to less experienced players.”

A warm-up tournament in New Zealand punctuated the Eagles’ eight-week pre-season. Since returning home the team has focused on refining systems, testing players and combinations, and elevating standards.

“We’ve come back into these two weeks of training hitting the ground running,” head coach Emilie Bydwell said. “We still have stuff that we need to clean up and can still be better. Our preseason was a long eight weeks before we were in New Zealand, and no matter how well it’s planned, it’s just not the same as playing.”

Kristi Kirshe resumes the role of team captain and oversees a Dubai squad that includes Olympian Ilona Maher.

“Beyond who she is as a player, she’s such a professional,” Bydwell said. “She takes what she does here very seriously, and she’s such a competitor. It’s been really great to have her back in — ready to compete, ready to drive the standards that we have as a team, and ready to empower the young athletes that she’s playing alongside.”

On the opposite end of the experience spectrum, Utahan teenager Fane Tausinga is traveling to the UAE in hopes of earning a first USA 7s cap.

The Dubai SVNS kicks off on Saturday, Nov. 28, and USA will compete in Pool A start against Spain (1 a.m. EST), followed by fellow New Zealand invitational attendees Australia (4:22 a.m.) and France (8:46 a.m.). Knockouts follow on Sunday, and all of the action will livestream on Paramount+.

title: Fiji names seven debutants for opening SVNS rounds
article_text:
Seven new faces have been included in the Fiji Airways Fijian men’s and Fijiana 7s squads for the opening two legs of the HSBC SVNS Series in Dubai and Cape Town.

The squads feature a blend of experienced campaigners and emerging talent, with debutants marked by an asterisk in the official team announcement.

In the Fijiana squad, captain Ana Naimasi will lead a side that includes Sesenieli Donu, Adi Salote Nailolo, Merewairita Neivosa, Laisani Mocesawana, Reapi Ulunisau, Varanisese Qoro, Kelerayani Luvu, Mariana Talatoka, Regan Chapman, Atelaite Ralivanawana, Ivi Savu and Mere Vocevoce.

The new caps in the women’s squad are Merewairita Neivosa and Regan Chapman.

For the men’s team, captain Tira Wilagi heads a squad featuring Akuila Dranivotua, Joseva Talacolo, Vilimone Raiqiso, Kavekini Tanivanuakula, George Bose, Aquino Savenaca, Douglas Daveta, Iowane Teba, Filipe Sauturaga, Sanaila Daliga, Vuiviwa Naduvalo and Saimone Qeleca.

The debutants in the men’s squad are Vilimone Raiqiso, Aquino Savenaca, Sanaila Daliga and Saimone Qeleca.

Both teams will begin their HSBC SVNS campaign in Dubai before travelling to Cape Town for the second tournament of the new season.

title: Hong Kong Open 2026: Lakshya Sen overcomes Loh Kean Yew in three games to enter semis
article_text:
Lakshya Sen beat Singapore’s Loh Kean Yew 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 to advance to the semifinals at the Hong Kong Open on Friday.

Lakshya made a brisk start to take an 11-7 lead into the interval, but Loh fought back strongly to draw level at 14-14. The two traded points in a tense finish before Lakshya found another gear to take the opening game 21-17.

Loh seized control early in the second game, racing to a 7-2 lead and carrying a comfortable 11-6 advantage into the interval. He continued to dominate after the break, stretching the lead to 19-10 before closing out the game 21-10 to force a decider.

Lakshya bounced back emphatically in the decider, racing to an 11-5 lead at the interval. He maintained his grip on the contest after the break, stretching the advantage to 19-10 before sealing the game 21-13 to complete a hard-fought victory.

Earlier, Lakshya, who is now assured of a spot at BWF Tour Finals 2026, beat Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke in straight games in the round of 16.

Lakshya revived his season in emphatic fashion, winning back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open and Japan Masters to emerge as a strong contender for the BWF World Tour Finals. His triumph in Japan, where he defeated Koki Watanabe in the final, proved crucial to his qualification bid, as he closed in on becoming only the second Indian after P. V. Sindhu (women’s singles) to make the cut for this year’s season-ending tournament.

Lakshya last featured in the BWF World Tour Finals in 2021, reaching the semifinals.

title: MLB’s Local Media Rights Emerge As Focus in Labor Fight
article_text:
The future of MLB’s local media business has become a central element in the sport’s labor battle, providing yet another substantial layer to the already fractious situation.

For the last six months, MLB club owners have proposed to pool the local media revenue of all 30 clubs as part of a sought-after economic system that would implement a hard salary cap and floor. Most recently, management has updated its cap offer to the MLB Players Association to a 2028 implementation, and vows there will be “no compromise” on the pursuit of a cap as the Dec. 1 expiration of the current labor deal and an expected lockout thereafter approach.

The pooling of local media revenues, and a promise to end regional blackouts that have long frustrated fans, were also part of a video recently distributed by MLB to fans.

Throughout the entrenched negotiations, though, two key questions have persisted: Why are the local media and salary cap issues so deeply linked, and why couldn’t owners just agree on their own to pool that revenue, similar to how the NFL operates?

The beginning of the answer lies in the accelerating economic divide between the local media revenue of well-heeled teams such as the Dodgers, Yankees, and Mets, and half the league that has lost traditional regional sports network rights deal entirely and now has its local games produced and distributed by MLB—often at less lucrative terms than what they had before.

That split, exacerbated by existential disruption across the media business, has been the key driver in a $446 million spending difference this year between the Dodgers’ total luxury-tax payroll and projected taxes, and the comparable figure for the Guardians.

The total pool of local media income in MLB has also fallen, with the roughly $2.4 billion in annual revenues earlier this decade now standing at about $1.8 billion. With a cap-based system, MLB believes it can both narrow the economic spread and enlarge the overall pie of local media revenue.

“We are trying to make changes to the game that fans want and will improve the value of our media rights,” MLB EVP of baseball operations Morgan Sword said in a presentation this week to reporters.

One of the teams whose games are produced by the league, the Brewers, won this year’s World Series, something Sword called out of step with the industry’s prevailing trends.

“It is truly aberrational in baseball for small markets to be successful,” he said. “It’s not impossible, but it is much, much more difficult in our sports than it is in any of the other sports.”

The second part of the question is more complicated. Pooling local media revenue has a direct connection to MLB’s revenue-sharing system, which is collectively bargained between the league and MLBPA due to its link to player compensation. In the current labor deal, teams currently pay 48% of their local revenue into a central pool. So the league says it cannot simply restructure this part of its economics without involving the union.

While that is indeed true, the blackouts remain a separate issue from a salary cap. A complete pooling of local media revenue, and an end to regional blackouts, could be negotiated with the union absent a salary cap, though that likely would create disruption in the current rights deals—something the league is reluctant to face.

Instead, management is seeking to achieve the local media pooling with a hard cap that players have long resisted. The league is also proposing several other sweeping changes in conjunction with the cap-and-floor system, including significant restrictions on free agency, a retooled draft, and a 154-game regular season.

“We’re not saying it’s the players’ fault there are blackouts. We’re also not saying a salary cap in isolation fixes blackouts,” Sword said. “What we are saying is that this economic system, which is a big series of trade-offs, for the clubs, for the players, enables us to do it.”

MLB additionally is looking to mimic the NBA’s recent strategy and pursue a much more nationalized strategy when its current rights deals expire after the 2028 season. The NBA did that to great success, nearly tripling its national deals to about $6.9 billion annually.

Amid all of that, the MLBPA has consistently argued that caps reduce overall player compensation, pit player against player in a zero-sum game, and erode contract covenants.

“There can be no clearer example of the league’s lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts,” MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer said in a statement. “There should be no illusions about the owners’ true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.”

title: TAB Replaces Aquis Australia as Gold Coast Turf Club Naming Rights Partner from November 2026
article_text:
TAB became the naming rights partner of the Gold Coast Turf Club effective November 1, 2026, in an agreement that runs through 2030. The venue’s official name changed to TAB PARK GOLD COAST TURF CLUB on that date, ending Aquis Australia’s nine-year tenure — a partnership that had been in place since 2017.

Tabcorp operates one of its largest next-generation retail venues at the Gold Coast site. The club’s CEO, Steve Lines, stated the club is working towards its ambition of becoming a metropolitan club, as acknowledged in the recent Racing Review and The Next Lap plan.

Steve Lines, GCTC CEO, stated the Club is working towards its ambition of becoming a metropolitan club as acknowledged in the recent Racing Review and The Next Lap plan.

The agreement between TAB and the Gold Coast Turf Club covers the period from November 1, 2026 to 2030. Aquis Australia’s nine-year tenure from 2017 to 2026 was described in source material as one of the longest-running venue naming rights partnerships in Australian sport.

Separately, Redcliffe Harness Racing Club appointed Chris Rose as business manager earlier in November 2026. Rose previously served on the committee of the Albion Park Harness Racing Club.

Mark McNee, president of Redcliffe Harness Racing Club, stated he has known Chris Rose for more than four decades. The appointment coincides with the club’s upcoming Saturday feature meeting on November 23, 2026, which will host the Redcliffe Yearling Sale Race Series Finals and the Chris Garrard Memorial.

The Redcliffe Yearling Sale Race Series 2YO Final on November 23, 2026 carries $125,000 in prize money. An additional $52,000 is on offer for the three-year-old division at the same meeting.

title: Wallabies make 5 changes to avoid 5th straight loss
Scotland injury update as Dempsey undergoes surgery but good news on Tuipulotu
article_text:
Jack Dempsey has undergone surgery on the foot injury he suffered against Australia, but there is better news concerning the fitness of captain Sione Tuipulotu.

The pair were ruled out of Scotland's final two Nations Championship fixtures this week after suffering foot and knee injuries, respectively.

Tuipulotu was a late withdrawal from the side to face Australia last weekend after aggravating the problem the day before the game.

On Tuesday, assistant coach Pieter de Villiers suggested Dempsey may need surgery on his foot problem.

And after naming his side to face Japan, Gregor Townsend confirmed the 32-year-old had gone under the knife.

"Jack got operated today so obviously he will be working with his club on that," said the Scotland coach.

"It's great that he's been able to have the surgery in Scotland and also very good that he's been operated so quickly and that he can make a quicker recovery."

Dempsey's injury is a significant setback to Dempsey, who will now miss a significant portion of the Top League season Toshiba Brave Lupus Tokyo.

But the prognosis for Tuipulotu is more encouraging, Townsend revealed, while also stating none of the other players who are injured are expected to miss the Six Nations.

"He flew down to see a specialist on Monday in London, so [he will be out for] three or four weeks.

"We're thinking Ben White's about the same time scale. Scott Cummings might be slightly longer and Fergus Burke is similar. Alex Craig had a hip issue and he didn't train fully leading up to New Zealand."

title: Dates Confirmed for Rugby World Cup 2031
article_text:
World Rugby has confirmed the tournament dates for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2031. The event will kick off on the weekend of October 3-5, 2031 with the final taking place on the weekend of November 14-16, 2031.

The announcement comes with attention firmly on Australia 2027 which is now well under a year away. The USA will compete at that tournament after missing out on France 2003 with losses to Chile and Portugal seeing a changing-up of competitors.

World Rugby’s move to expand the Men’s Rugby World Cup from 20 to 24 teams has come as a safeguard against the 2031 hosts not being involved in the 2027 tournament. The USA and, potential co-hosts Canada, will both compete at Rugby World Cup 2027.

As noted by World Rugby, by this time next year the USA will be hosting baton. The year 2027 will see plenty of progress towards the staging of Rugby World Cup 2031. For example, host cities and venues will be processed ahead of an announcement in early 2028.

Organizers are presently in talks with NFL and MLS venues ahead of the 2028 announcement. The tournament dates of October 3-5 to November 14-16, 2031 mean that there will be a cross-over between the Rugby World Cup and the NFL season.

title: Scotland's £70,000 World Rugby fine explained
article_text:
Scottish Rugby were fined £70,000 in 2019 over comments made about World Rugby before their controversial Rugby World Cup clash against Japan.

The Pool A fixture was in doubt due to the approach of Typhoon Hagibis, with its cancellation potentially ending Scotland's hopes of reaching the quarter-finals.

Former SRU chief executive Mark Dodson, who stepped down in 2024, hit out at World Rugby's "rigidity" over the situation and hinted at legal action if the match was called off.

An independent disputes committee subsequently ruled that his comments amounted to misconduct and "brought the game into disrepute".

"Prior to its decision, the committee gave the parties ample time to resolve the dispute," it said in a statement.

"World Rugby made an open offer to the SRU, which required the SRU to apologise for its conduct and make a donation to the typhoon disaster relief fund in Japan.

"The SRU suggested alternative wording, which included a mutual expression of regret from both parties - and no apology."

Scottish Rugby was formally reprimanded, fined £70,000 and ordered to "issue in writing a meaningful apology to World Rugby and RWCL for its misconduct in terms approved by the committee".

The governing body had initially rejected World Rugby's proposed settlement, which included an apology and a donation towards typhoon relief efforts.

"World Rugby strongly believed the comments, which suggested an unfair and disorganised treatment of all teams, to be inappropriate and ill-judged at a time when Japan was preparing for the largest and most destructive typhoon in decades," a statement said.

"The international federation believed that such comments brought the game into disrepute, not only in relation to World Rugby's handling of an extraordinary situation but also in the message that it sent to the Japanese people."

The £70,000 fine was directed towards World Rugby's ChildFund Pass It Back programme, supporting communities affected by the typhoon.

The match eventually went ahead, with Scotland suffering a 28-21 defeat to Japan. The result saw them eliminated from the tournament before the quarter-finals.

Following the ruling, Scottish Rugby said: "we will now reflect on this outcome and further consider all our options, which may include arbitration".

The dispute was eventually resolved on 14 November 2019, with Scottish Rugby expressing regret and agreeing to make a £70,000 donation.

title: Alcaraz Cleared to Continue ATP Finals, But Risk Remains
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has reportedly received encouraging news regarding his left hamstring injury and has decided to continue competing at the ATP Finals in Turin.

According to reports from Spanish media, including Punto de Break, Cadena COPE and RTVE, an MRI conducted on Thursday ruled out structural damage to the Spaniard’s left hamstring, clearing the way for him to face Flavio Cobolli on Friday.

Note: Alcaraz has already qualified for the semifinals, so the stakes of Friday’s match aren’t as high as they might have been had he been preparing to play for qualifying for the semifinals.

It doesn’t necessarily mean the 23-year-old, who cancelled today’s practice with junior No.1 Guto Miguel of Brazil, is out of the woods.

Cadena SER reports that Alcaraz’s team is taking a cautious, match-by-match approach, with the seven-time Grand Slam champion expected to evaluate his physical condition following Friday’s encounter before making any decisions about the semifinals.

Friday’s match with Cobolli should give him the information he needs to decide whether or not he feels good enough to make a run at winning the title in Turin.

There is also the matter of Alcaraz’s right knee, which had been troubling him ahead of the tournament. RTVE reported that Thursday’s medical examinations also addressed the knee, but no specific findings have been made public.

It all adds up to a delicate situation for Alcaraz, who has plenty at stake beyond this week’s competition in Turin. The Spaniard is expected to represent his country at the Davis Cup Finals later this month, and the pressure to compete for his nation will undoubtedly weigh heavily on him.

There is also the bigger picture to consider.

With the 2027 season fast approaching, Alcaraz will have a relatively short offseason to recover, rebuild and prepare for his Australian Open title defense.

But the combination of hamstring discomfort and an ongoing knee concern makes this an especially important moment for the Spaniard. Tempted by winning the ATP Finals and then representing Spain at Davis Cup could come at a cost. He’ll have to listen closely to his body, and make a decision that balances the present and the future.

title: De Minaur to headline major Australian tournament amid form slump
article_text:
Alex de Minaur will take part in the Brisbane International for the first time in eight years, announcing he will play the Australian Open lead-up tournament in January.

In doing so, he becomes the biggest marquee player to sign up for the event since Rafael Nadal, Novak Djokovic and Andy Murray did so across the early 2020s.

It is also the event where Nick Kyrgios made his fleeting attempt at a singles return in 2026, before opting out of an Australian Open wildcard spot.

The tournament gets underway in the first week of January and de Minaur is excited to build into what will be a crucial calendar year for him.

“I love playing on Pat Rafter Arena and have so many fond memories of competing in Brisbane. The support is always awesome, and I can’t wait to get back out there,” de Minaur said.

“There’s nothing better than playing at home in Australia. The first week of the year is a great opportunity to get the season off to a strong start, and Brisbane is the perfect place to do that.

“It’ll be a strong field, as always, but you can’t beat winning at home, so I’ll be doing everything I can to lift the trophy in Brisbane.”

It marks the starting point of what the 27-year-old hopes will be a form turning point, after a difficult 2026 season.

De Minaur will enter 2027 as the No.11 ranked player in the world, after being as high as fifth in July.

A second round exit at the US Open coupled with poor performances on the ATP Tour in the second half of the year ultimately cost him from a ranking perspective.

The Aussie admits he has to change his mindset going forward and learn from what has turned into a form slump.

“It’s the first time that I’ve felt the inconsistency,” de Minaur told the Associated Press.

“I went through a six-month period where I kind of went walkabout. I wasn’t myself. I wasn’t playing the type of tennis that I know I could and I missed out on a lot of opportunities.

“I’ve been spoiled in a way that I’ve been able to bring that level week in and week out and for the longest time I almost expected those wins.

“I’ve got to be a little bit nicer to myself and appreciative of winning any sort of match.

“I was still worried about the level I was playing and I wasn’t content with myself.

“That carried on to the whole clay season and then it became a little bit of a snowball effect.”

Performance on the big stage in Grand Slams has also come into focus for de Minaur.

Despite sitting in-and-around the top 10 since 2023, he has had a tendency to stumble when it matters most.

De Minaur is yet to advance beyond a Grand Slam quarter-final at any of the four majors to this point of his career.

He made the quarter-final in the 2026 Australian Open before losing to Carlos Alcaraz, and stumbled in early phases of the other three Slams, missing out on golden opportunities to advance deep while Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner missed time with injuries.

“That’s one of the key things I want to focus on and try to go deep at the Slams,” he said.

“Really try to prioritise that a little bit more to make sure that all my energy goes towards those events.”

He has made the last two Australian Open quarter-finals, and will be hoping 2027 is the year he pushes deeper on his home turf.

title: ATP Finals 2026 Day 5 Recap
article_text:
Day 5 of the 2026 ATP Finals saw Alexander Zverev complete a perfect round-robin campaign, while Ben Shelton booked his place in the semi-finals after a hard-fought victory over Rafael Jodar.

Shelton survived two set points in a tight opening-set tiebreak before eventually seeing off the Spaniard in straight sets, although he had to wait for the evening result to confirm his qualification.

Zverev then defeated Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6), despite the Frenchman saving five consecutive match points in a dramatic second-set tiebreak. The German tops the John McEnroe Group with three wins from three and hasn’t dropped a service game all week.

The result sets up a semi-final between Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz, while Zverev will face the winner of Friday’s clash between Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe.

Both Zverev and Alcaraz look a level above the rest so far, although a few physical concerns remain heading into the knockout stages, with Alcaraz nursing a hamstring issue and Zverev also appearing uncomfortable towards the end of his match.

Ben Shelton (3) def. Rafael Jodar (8) 7-6(8), 7-5

Ben Shelton kept his ATP Finals semi-final hopes alive on Thursday afternoon, defeating Rafael Jodar 7-6(8), 7-5 in a hard-fought encounter.

The American, who lost to Alexander Zverev on Tuesday, had to work considerably harder than expected against the 20-year-old Spaniard, eventually coming through in two hours and seven minutes.

The opening set was closely contested, with Jodar putting Shelton under pressure on serve and creating break opportunities. However, the American escaped trouble with his usual big serving, and the pair eventually headed to a tiebreak.

Jodar had two set points in the breaker, but Shelton saved both before finally taking it 10-8 when the Spaniard framed a forehand long.

The second set was another tight affair, though Shelton looked to have taken control after moving up to 4-2. However, Jodar refused to go away, fighting back to level at 5-5 with aggressive baseline hitting.

At that point, it looked like we might be heading for another tiebreak, but Shelton produced one of his better return games to break at 5-5, moving Jodar from corner to corner before serving out the match.

It wasn’t really a convincing display from Shelton from the baseline, and he basically relied heavily on his serve to get himself out of trouble.

Jodar had plenty of opportunities and probably should have taken the opening set, but he looked a bit leggy, especially when moving forward to track down Shelton’s shorter slices.

Jodar finishes his ATP Finals debut with three defeats, but his rise from No. 168 at the start of the year to the world’s top ten is one of the season’s stories, and he’s certainly one to watch next year.

Shelton, meanwhile, finishes the round-robin stage at 2-1 and must now wait for the result of Alexander Zverev’s match against Arthur Fils.

If Fils wins in straight sets, the Frenchman will progress alongside Zverev. Any other result will see Shelton qualify for the semi-finals in second place.

Alexander Zverev (1) def. Arthur Fils 6-4 7-6(6)

Alexander Zverev completed a perfect round-robin campaign at the 2026 ATP Finals on Thursday evening, defeating Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6) to finish top of the John McEnroe Group without dropping a set.

The World No. 1, who had already secured his semi-final spot with victories over Rafael Jodar and Ben Shelton, made a solid start against the Frenchman, relying on his excellent serving and consistent baseline game.

Fils played some decent tennis in the opening set, but a sloppy service game at 3-3 proved costly. Zverev converted his third break point to move 4-3 ahead and comfortably served out the set 6-4 in around 35 minutes, ending Fils’ hopes of reaching the semi-finals and confirming Shelton’s qualification.

However, I liked how Fils tried to play, and he wasn’t about to roll over as the second set proved far more competitive.

The Frenchman raised his level, going toe-to-toe with Zverev from the baseline (who I thought didn’t hit his forehand as well), and showing the aggressive tennis that has propelled him into the Top 8 despite posting a woeful Grand Slam record.

Neither player could find the breakthrough until Fils earned two set points on Zverev’s serve at 6-5. However, Sascha produced some huge serves to escape trouble and force a tiebreak.

Zverev then won six consecutive points to lead 6-1, seemingly putting the match to bed, but Fils remarkably saved five straight match points to level at 6-6.

However, Sascha eventually got the job done, taking the breaker 8-6 to seal another straight-sets victory.

Fils put in a decent effort, and if he’d been a little wiser on some points, he’d have taken a set, but he ultimately couldn’t get past Zverev when it mattered.

For the German, it’s been an excellent group stage. Three matches, three victories, and six sets won without dropping a single one. He’s also gone through all three matches without losing a service game, which is pretty impressive given the opposition, but not so surprising given he’s bombing down 185 km/h second serves, on average.

Zverev advances to the semi-finals as the John McEnroe Group winner and will face either Daniil Medvedev or Frances Tiafoe, who meet on Friday to decide the second qualifying spot from the Ivan Lendl Group.

Shelton also advances despite his Tuesday defeat to Zverev and will face Carlos Alcaraz in the other semi-final.

title: Alexander Zverev suffers injury scare as Carlos Alcaraz discovers his fate at ATP Finals
article_text:
Alexander Zverev cleared some of the fog around the group phase of the ATP Finals as he powered to a third successive straight sets win by seeing off the challenge of Arthur Fils in Turin.

Zverev highlighted his impressive record against top ten rivals who are not Jannik Sinner or Carlos Alcaraz in a press conference earlier this week and he has backed up those words by adding another three wins to his record this week.

Zverev has seen off Rafael Jodar, Ben Shelton and now Fils in convincing fashion, with his latest win ensuring Shelton will progress to a potential semi-final clash against Alcaraz on Saturday.

There are doubts over whether Alcaraz will compete in the latter stages of the ATP Finals after he injured his hamstring in his win against Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday, but he now knows another match against Shelton awaits if he is fit enough to compete.

Alcaraz went for a scan on his hamstring on Thursday morning and it has been decided that he will try to compete in the rest of the tournament, but that position could change if his condition worsens.

Zverev also suffered an injury scare in his win against Fils, as he admitted a long-standing ankle problem was giving him some concern.

The pain he feels is linked to the huge injury he suffered in his 2022 French Open semi-final against Rafael Nadal, as he conceded it still gives him pain.

“Unfortunately I started feeling my ankle again,” Zverev said after his 6-4, 7-6(6) victory.

“I’ll probably feel my ankle sometimes until the end of my career. Unfortunately, the injury that I had was quite big. I’m going to do everything that I can to be pain-free on Saturday, but this is something I have to live with nowadays.”

Zverev also admitted some of his intensity was lacking against Fils as he knew his place in the semi-finals was already secured.

“I thought the first two matches were very high level,” he added.

“Today I thought I played a little bit worse from the baseline, but I’m very happy to have won all three matches, against three very difficult opponents.

“Arthur, for me personally, is a very difficult opponent because of how much power he has, but I’m happy to be through in straight sets.”

Zverev is set to play Daniil Medvedev in the last four on Saturday, with Alcaraz taking on Shelton if he can manage his hamstring problem.

title: Miyazaki avenges Akechi and faces Wang in Hong Kong Open semifinals
article_text:
Tomoka Miyazaki, Japan's next-generation women's badminton star and the world No. 7, swept past compatriot Hina Akechi, ranked No. 14, to avenge her loss at the Korea Open and reach the Hong Kong Open semifinals.

Miyazaki beat Akechi 2-0 (21-11, 21-9) in the women's singles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500) on the 20th at Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong.

It was a dominant victory. Miyazaki trailed 4-2 early in the first game but reeled off five straight points to take a 7-4 lead. She extended it to 10-5, and when Akechi began to close the gap, Miyazaki scored five consecutive points again to go ahead 15-6. She eventually took the first game 21-11.

The second game followed a similar pattern. Leading 2-1 early on, Miyazaki won seven points in a row to go up 9-1. Akechi fought back to 13-8, but Miyazaki won five straight points to seal the momentum. She closed out the match 21-9.

The victory means more than simply reaching the semifinals. On the 6th, Miyazaki lost to Akechi in the Korea Open women's singles quarterfinals in Yeosu, South Jeolla province, falling 2-1 (13-21, 23-21, 21-8) after taking the first game.

The Hong Kong Open is a good opportunity for Miyazaki to contend for the title. The top three in the women's singles rankings — world No. 1 Ahn Se-young, No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi of Japan and No. 5 Pusarla Venkata Sindhu of India — are all absent.

Miyazaki has already secured a spot in the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals. If she wins her first title of the season at this tournament, she can build her confidence ahead of the season-ending finals next month.

Miyazaki will face Wang Zhiyi in the semifinals. Wang beat Indonesia's Putri Kusuma Wardani 2-0 (22-20, 22-20) in an earlier quarterfinal.

After avenging her Korea Open loss to Akechi, Miyazaki now has a chance to get back at Wang Zhiyi, who eliminated her at the Kumamoto Masters. She is just two wins away from her first title of the season.

title: An Se-young and Yamaguchi both absent, China suffers 'massive humiliation' as women's singles players eliminated one after another... Wang Zhiyi is already the sole survivor
article_text:
*This content was translated by AI.View Original

Neither Korea's badminton "queen" An Se-young (24, Samsung Life) nor Japan's star Yamaguchi Akane (29) are present. However, China suffered humiliation as its women's singles players were eliminated one after another. Wang Zhiyi (26) is already the only one left standing.

World No. 3 Wang Zhiyi defeated Nidaara Natuki (Japan) 2-0 (21-13, 21-15) in the women's singles round of 16 at the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500), held on the 19th (Korean time) at the Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong. Among the four Chinese players who entered the women's singles event at this tournament, Wang Zhiyi is the only one to advance to the quarterfinals.

From China's perspective, this tournament was an opportunity they absolutely did not want to miss. This is because world No. 1 An Se-young and No. 2 Yamaguchi were both absent.

An Se-young has been combining rest and treatment since winning the Korea Open on the 8th of last month. She is in the process of getting her body in shape ahead of the BWF World Tour Finals, which will be held in Hangzhou, China, next month.

At the "Yonex Podium Day with Badminton National Team" event held at The Hyundai Seoul in Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul on the 16th of last month, An Se-young shared her recent status, saying, "I have been running without rest for three months, so my body has broken down quite a bit and I am receiving treatment."

An Se-young's absence was a huge opportunity for other players. This season, An Se-young recorded 71 wins and one loss in 72 matches, and she had run up a streak of 55 consecutive victories since her defeat in the All England Open final in March of last year. She has already collected 11 championship trophies.

On top of that, Yamaguchi also did not participate in this tournament. Yamaguchi is a powerhouse who won the Kumamoto Masters on the 15th of last month by consecutively defeating Chinese players.

At the time, Chen Yufei withdrew due to a foot injury during the final game of the semifinal against Yamaguchi. Wang Zhiyi, who advanced to the final, also lost to Yamaguchi 0-2 (14-21, 20-22). China had aimed for victory in a tournament where An Se-young was absent, but they were blocked by another wall.

At this Hong Kong Open, both players were avoided, but China's challenge is not unfolding as expected. Sina.com explained, "China sent out all its main women's singles players, but rivals An Se-young and Yamaguchi did not participate," adding, "Wang Zhiyi and Chen Yufei received the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds respectively, so the outlook for winning was very bright."

However, contrary to expectations, Chinese players packed their bags one after another. The media pointed out, "Only Wang Zhiyi remains in China's women's singles."

The biggest shock was the elimination of world No. 4 Chen Yufei. Chen Yufei lost to Lakshita Ramraj (India), ranked 47th in the world, 0-2 (18-21, 22-24) in the round of 16 on the same day. The Tokyo Olympics women's singles gold medalist failed to win a single game against the 19th-year-old promising player.

Just one day earlier, she had shown confidence. According to China's Xinhua News Agency, Chen Yufei was asked about the drought in Chinese women's singles titles after defeating Amalie Schulz (Denmark) on the 18th of last month.

In response, Chen Yufei said, "I think this tournament will be fine." However, her own challenge ended in her second match.

Her foot injury, which is still recovering, and a tight schedule were also variables. Sina.com assessed, "Chen Yufei looked relatively tired throughout the match, and her movement on the court was not agile enough."

It further analyzed, "The previous injury and this tight schedule appear to have had some impact on Chen Yufei." Chen Yufei played her first-round match the previous evening and then returned to the court somewhat earlier than other players on that day.

Another Chinese player, Han We, also could not continue the tournament to the end. She withdrew in the round of 16 against Michelle Li (Canada) due to physical condition issues. She had lost the first game 14-21 and was trailing 5-11 in the second game.

Shi Wenjing had already been eliminated after losing to Akechi Hina (Japan) in the first round. With Chen Yufei and Han We also withdrawing in the round of 16, the challenge for a Chinese women's singles title has fallen solely on Wang Zhiyi.

Victory is desperately needed in Chinese women's singles. They have not been able to lift a trophy for a full eight months. Wang Zhiyi has not reached the top since the All England Open in March of last year, and Chen Yufei's only win this year was at the Indonesia Masters in January of this year. The shoulders of Wang Zhiyi, who is left alone, are inevitably even heavier.

Wang Zhiyi will face Putri Kusuma Wardani (Indonesia) in the quarterfinals on the 20th. As the sole survivor in Chinese women's singles, she will challenge for a spot in the semifinals.

title: What to make of Tiger Woods' return to golf at Hero World Classic, Bryson DeChambeau's move to DP World Tour
article_text:
The DP World Tour's 2027 season came to end this past weekend with Rory McIlroy claiming the Race to Dubai and Tyrrell Hatton running away with the DP World Tour Championship. Hatton's victory came one week after his former LIV Golf mate, Jon Rahm, won the Abu Dhabi Championship as the reassimilation of those who left the European circuit only to return a few years later is well underway.

It is not just Europeans, however, who are flocking to the DP World Tour, but also Bryson DeChambeau. News surfaced Tuesday that he has The inclusion of these players will beef up the DP World Tour next season, but is there another angle we should consider?

The PGA Tour wraps up its season this weekend at the RSM Classic in Sea Island, Georgia, while Tiger Woods will begin a new season of his career next month at the Hero World Challenge. Will this comeback be any different, or should we frame it in a new light given his off-the-course issues?

The game keeps moving, and CBS Sports is keeping up with it as we dive into the most pressing issues and conversation points with the newest edition of The Three Putt.

After winning his eighth Race to Dubai crown, McIlroy mentioned how difficult it will be to repeat (again) in 2027. Well, lo and behold, the gates of LIV Golf have brought a flood of former and new members to the DP World Tour with DeChambeau leading the charge.

Following years of carrying the water for LIV Golf, DeChambeau will be able to access any tournament of his choosing on the DP World Tour next season thanks to his 2024 U.S Open win. What do you think of the move at large?

Robby Kalland: It was really his only play, so it's not surprising, but I am extremely intrigued by what the DP World Tour can be next year. The challenge the DP World Tour has faced in recent years is that their best players defect to the PGA Tour every year, with the top 10 all earning cards. Next year, they are going to have their usual crop plus an influx of LIV stars waiting out their year-long suspension from returning to the PGA Tour (barring a sudden change of heart from the bosses in Ponte Vedra).

DeChambeau, Rahm, Hatton & Co. will suddenly be tournament staples. We've already seen Rahm and Hatton win this fall, and Patrick Reed dominated early in 2026 after leaving LIV Golf. Will we see DeChambeau, Rahm and Hatton all collect trophies in 2027? Will there be a bit more parity than expected on the international circuit? These are some outstanding questions.

Patrick McDonald: All of this comes at such an interesting time. The PGA Tour and DP World Tour are deep in negotiations regarding the new strategic alliance ahead of changes coming in 2028. One point of contention appears to be how many cards will be awarded to the top finishers on the DP World Tour; four is rumored to be the magic number for the Championship Series.

It feels safe to say players like Hatton and Niemann (depending on how many starts the latter gets) will contend for those, leaving just a couple for the DP World Tour faithful. All of this to say, yes, the LIV alumni should play well, win trophies, grow the game in the far corners of the world and put the last five years behind them, but the trickle-down effects from this move could be more compelling.

One man we know won't be competing on the DP World Tour next year is Tiger, but the Big Cat is making his return next month at his event in the Bahamas, the Hero World Challenge. We haven't seen Woods play outdoor golf since 2024, and he's had more surgeries (and more off-course trouble) since then. What are your expectations for Tiger's latest comeback, and how differently do you feel about this return compared to others?

McDonald: I swear we are stuck in a "Groundhog Day"-like time loop; we are always left talking about Tiger and a potential comeback this time of year. His game is gone when stacked against Scottie Scheffler and the lot, but the major schedule has to motivate him for 2027 with stops at Pebble Beach and St. Andrews on the docket. Beyond that, he has to be eyeing the all-time USGA championship record, as he is tied with Bobby Jones for the most all-time with nine.

If that is his North Star, and he is competing against the olds, I am more optimistic than the song and dance of the last five or so years, which has been tough to watch and sometimes sad to follow. What say you?

Kalland: Last year was the first of my life that neither Tiger nor Phil Mickelson played in a major, and at the risk of getting excommunicated from the golf writer world ... dare I say ... it was borderline refreshing?

Those two defined golf for so long, and when it was what they were doing on the golf course, the sport was arguably the best it's ever been. Unfortunately, that duo has produced far more headlines for controversies off of it recently, and the dominant feeling for me around Woods' latest return is best described as trepidation.

I hope it works out. I hope his body can hold up. I hope this latest DUI and rollover car crash was a legitimate wake-up call for him to get a better handle on things. However, the entire time, we'll all be wondering when the other shoe will drop -- whether with an injury or something else that happens away from the course.

title: RSM Classic: Billy Horschel faces setback over PGA Tour future after slow start, as Jesper Svensson races ahead
article_text:
Sweden's Jesper Svensson holds a one-shot lead after the opening round of the RSM Classic, the final PGA Tour event of the season; Brooks Koepka is five strokes back and Billy Horschel is seven behind; watch the second round live on Friday from 1.30pm on Sky Sports Golf

Jesper Svensson produced a late burst to grab the early lead at the RSM Classic, as Billy Horschel made a slow start to his bid to retain full PGA Tour playing rights.

Only the top 100 in the FedExCup standings after this week's event in St Simons Island remain fully exempt on the PGA Tour, with Horschel heading into the week 101st and projected to fall further down the rankings after opening with a one-under 71.

Horschel - an eight-time winner on the PGA Tour - carded three birdies and two bogeys on the Plantation Course, one of two used at Sea Island Golf Club, to leave him seven strokes behind Svensson.

Svensson birdied eight of his last 11 holes on the same course as Horschel - including each of his last four - to post an eight-under 64 and move into a one-shot lead, with Max Greyserman and Garrick Higgo sharing second after opening 65s.

Michael Thorbjornsen posted the lowest round on the Seaside Course, with a six-under 64 leaving him tied-fourth alongside Emiliano Grillo, Hank Lebioda, Maverick McNealy, Lee Hodges and Davis Riley.

Ramsus Hojgaard and Marco Penge, entering the week outside the top 100 in the season-long standings, sit in the group on four under alongside Ryder Cup player Sepp Straka - who finished inside top 50 during the regular season.

Koepka described his season as a "disappointment" ahead of this week's event, with the five-time major champion opening with a three-under 67, while England's John Parry - entering the week 96th in the ranking - started with a two-under 70.

All players ranked No 51 and below carry their FedExCup points over from the regular season and first play-off event into the 'FedExCup Fall', giving them the chance to boost their status for next season.

Those 51st to 60th after this week qualify for the first two Signature Events of 2027, while those who end between 101st and 125th on the PGA Tour only receive conditional status and be unable to feature in certain events.

Players outside the top 125 face a season on the Korn Ferry Tour or a trip to Q-School to earn their PGA Tour playing rights, with first-round leader Svensson entering the week in 135th spot.

Who will win the RSM Classic? Watch throughout the week live on Sky Sports. Live coverage continues Friday with Featured Groups from 1.30pm on Sky Sports Golf ahead of full coverage from 5pm. Get the latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract.

title: Here’s the prize money payout for each golfer at the LPGA’s 2026 CME Group Tour Championship
article_text:
Just like on the PGA Tour, the LPGA season is ending this week. But, unlike what’s happening up in Georgia, $4 million will go to the winner of the CME Group Tour Championship. The total purse is $11 million at Tiburon Golf Club in Naples, with the biggest winner’s check on tour going to the first-place finisher.

Nelly Korda and Jeeno Thitikul, World Nos. 1 and 2, are the ones to beat, but winning multiple times this season. Korda, however, won two majors while Thitikul is still looking for her first. However, she is the two-time defending champion this week after winning each of the last two years.

Korda, like last week, has another chance at earning entrance into the LPGA’s Hall of Fame. Only a victory will get here there.

The 60-player field is made up of 17 of the 19 winners on tour this season. That includes Lindy Duncan, a popular first-time winner last week at the Annika Sorenstam event outside Tampa. In all, there are 20 of the top 25 players in the world competing.

Check back here Sunday when play is complete for updates on the money below.

title: Jesper Svensson catches fire late to seize early lead at The RSM Classic
article_text:
ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. (AP) — Michael Thorbjornsen spent the last few weeks working on his iron play and saw it pay off Thursday in the rain and wind at Sea Island. He made five of his seven birdies inside 10 feet for a 6-under 64 and the low score on the Seaside Course to trail Sweden's Jesper Svensson, who played the Plantation Course, by two shots at The RSM Classic.

Thorbjornsen, one of the group of rising young stars who won the Rocket Classic this year for his first PGA Tour title, had five birdies in a seven-hole stretch around the turn at the tougher Seaside Course (par 70), which included an 8-foot par save.

Michael Thorbjornsen's 146-yard approach sets up birdie on No. 11 at The RSM

Svensson, who needs at least a two-way tie for second to finish among the top 100 in the FedExCup to keep a full card for next year, birdied his last four holes on the easier Plantation Course (par 72) for an 8-under 64. He entered the week No. 135 in the FedExCup standings.

The final tournament of the PGA Tour season brings different levels of pressure, mainly for those who want to be fully exempt next year by finishing in the top 100.

“Everybody knows what they need to do out there,” Grillo said after a 66 at Plantation. “Yeah, good start. Hopefully many more of these. I know what I need to do and it was good.”

Thorbjornsen is among nine players in the field who finished in the top 50 on the PGA Tour and are exempt for all of the $20 million Signature Events in 2027. He felt the missing piece was his iron game, not giving himself enough birdie chances.

“We've worked very hard on my irons, just having more control,” Thorbjornsen said. “My driving stats have been pretty decent these past couple years and I haven’t really been able to take advantage of it. So trying to get the ball closer to the hole. That gives you more birdie looks but also less bogey chances.”

Ten of the top 16 players on the leaderboard to par came into the week outside the top 100 in the FedExCup standings. Thirty-five spots outside of the magic number, Svensson spent most of his day trying to keep himself and his golf clubs dry and negotiating a wind that wasn't as strong as practice rounds but no less a nuisance.

The Swede had seven birdies on the back nine at Plantation and only wants to keep going.

“You can’t really deny the situation that you’re in,” Svensson said. “Not really thinking of it when you’re playing as much as trying to hit the right areas and hit some good shots. That’s number one task really and see where that takes me.”

Brooks Koepka has been working with new coaches, including Brad Faxon with his putting that hurt him so much this year. Playing for the first time in six weeks, the five-time major champion opened with a 67 on Seaside.

Brooks Koepka holes 59-foot shot for birdie on No. 14 at The RSM

Blades Brown, at No. 54 in the world and hopeful of a late push to get into the Masters by the end of the year, had a pair of birdies late in his round to salvage a 1-under 69 at Seaside. Ben James, the PGA Tour University's No. 1 player in 2026 who is one spot behind Brown in the world ranking, shot 4-under 68 at Plantation.

Thorbjornsen and Mitchell head to the easier Plantation on Friday. They were the only players in the top 10 on the leaderboard who played Seaside in the opening round.

title: PGA Tour winner misses crucial opportunity after injury forces season-ending exit
article_text:
Two-time PGA Tour winner Erik van Rooyen will not earn conditional status for the 2027 season after being forced to withdraw from the final event of the season with injury.

The big South African pulled out of the RSM Classic on Thursday morning because of a rib injury, the PGA Tour confirmed.

Six-time Tour winner Bill Haas was drafted into the field at Sea Island Resort as his replacement.

Van Rooyen had entered the tournament with hopes of improving his position in the FedExCup Fall standings and securing conditional status for next season.

The 34-year-old had enjoyed an encouraging run of form in recent weeks, recording top-10 finishes in two of his previous three starts, including a tie for fourth at last week's Austin Championship.

Those results lifted him to 125th in the points standings, putting him in contention to secure playing opportunities for 2027.

However, his withdrawal means he is now projected to miss out on conditional status, dealing a significant blow to his hopes of retaining playing privileges on the PGA Tour.

Haas, meanwhile, was a late replacement after an eventful week of travel.

The American had attempted to qualify for the tournament through Monday's qualifier but finished one shot outside a play-off for the final two available places.

Golf Channel reported that Haas made a five-hour drive home, only to be informed that a space in the field was on offer at the last minute.

He made the journey back to south Georgia on Wednesday and was confirmed as a replacement for Van Rooyen, giving him the opportunity to make just his third PGA Tour appearance of the year.

The RSM Classic is the final tournament of the PGA Tour's fall schedule.

More than a dozen changes had already been made to the field since Monday, with the late withdrawal of Van Rooyen providing another reminder of the uncertainty surrounding the tournament's line-up.

Former champion Ludvig Aberg was among those to withdraw. The Swede tweaked his back, but a subsequent MRI scan revealed no serious damage had been done.

Several big names are in danger of losing full status for the 2027 season.

Only the top 100 players in the rankings earn full cards.

Billy Horschel, Marco Penge, Joel Dahmen and former U.S. Open champion Lucas Glover are among the notables in danger of losing full status.
